objections: [mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The narrower form that is safe: SPLIT IT. Commit A deletes only Volt.Engine/Graphical/PouToXml.cs — that half is genuinely inert, needs no other file touched (SDK globbing), and needs no test edit at all (the guard's allowlist is consulted only against files that exist, so a stale entry cannot fail it). Commit B removes the BodyLanguage fields, and only after re-auditing ALL FOUR construction sites: Materializer.cs:58, :75 (named args — safe), :93, and :160 (positional, 10 args — MISSING from the move). If it proceeds as one commit anyway, the single thing to watch is Materializer.cs:93-94: delete the `parsed.BodyLanguage ?? "ST"` argument, NOT `body`. Removing `body` compiles clean because "ST" binds to `string? BodyText`, and the result is the literal text `ST` written as every POU's body into the user's repo on the next pull. Convert that site to NAMED arguments (`new PouData(Kind: kind, Declaration: declaration.Trim(), BodyText: body, Children: children)`) before deleting anything, so the compiler — not the reviewer's eye — enforces the mapping. Also drop the "the allowlist edit is REQUIRED or the guard fails" claim from the move text: it is false, and a shape move should not carry a justification that does not survive reading the test.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone / builds as written): the move's edit list is incomplete. It names three BodyLanguage population sites in Materializer (:58, :75, :93) but there is a FOURTH — the positional ChildData construction at Materializer.cs:160-162 (`new ChildData(ItemKind.Kinds.Property, childName, ide.ReadDeclaration(child).Trim(), null, null, folder, getterCode, setterCode, getterDecl, setterDecl)` — 10 positional args, the 4th being BodyLanguage). Applied exactly as written, the solution does not compile. Consequence: the commit as specified is red; the implementer has to discover and fix a site the move never audited, which is exactly the class of miss that turns a 'pure deletion' into an improvised edit.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (blast radius under-declared): the move row's `files` field lists ONLY PouToXml.cs, while its `what` deletes fields from Volt.Engine/Workspace/PouData.cs and forces edits in Volt.Engine/Workspace/Materializer.cs (4 sites) and, per target.md, test/Volt.Engine.Tests/WireVocabularyGuardTests.cs. Three of the four touched files are absent from the row a reviewer is given.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (nothing observable changes) — NOT PROVEN SAFE at Materializer.cs:93-94. `return new PouData(kind, declaration.Trim(), parsed.BodyLanguage ?? "ST", body, children);` — after BodyLanguage is dropped the record becomes (Kind, Declaration, BodyText, Children), and deleting the WRONG adjacent argument (`body` instead of `parsed.BodyLanguage ?? "ST"`) still COMPILES CLEAN: `"ST"` binds to `string? BodyText`. The result is that every POU materializes with the literal body `ST` and that text is committed to the user's git repo on the next pull. The move's own 'riskiest part' claims arity change makes the risk 'loud, not silent' — at this one site it is precisely silent. (The other two nullary sites, :58 and :160, are harmless either way.)

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (test edits) — the move mandates a test edit on a FALSE premise. target.md asserts: 'The allowlist edit is REQUIRED in the same commit or WireVocabularyGuardTests fails on a missing file.' Read the guard: WireVocabularyGuardTests.cs:72-74 enumerates existing files under src/ and skips those whose filename is in the allowlist (`allow.Contains(Path.GetFileName(file))`). Nothing ever validates that an allowlist entry names a file that exists. A stale "PouToXml.cs" entry is inert and the test stays green. The stated justification for touching a guard test is wrong; the edit is optional hygiene, not a build requirement.

moves.title: Repoint two round-trip tests at the shipped ST emitter and delete StAssembler
moves.what: Change `ChildDirectiveTests.cs:39` and `InterfaceRoundTripTests.cs:29` from `StAssembler.Assemble(dictionary)` to building a `PouData` and calling `PouToStText.Convert`. Delete `Volt.Engine/Workspace/SourceText/StAssembler.cs` (211) and the `ponytail:` note at :32-35, which prescribes exactly this once those two tests move.
moves.why: The canonical workspace-ST emit format — the exact bytes the content hash and every git diff are taken over — lives in two files, and the two round-trip tests certify the copy that ships to nobody. They have ALREADY diverged in failure policy: `PouToStText.cs:49-60` throws `INVALID_CODE_HEADER` with the comment 'an invented END_<KIND> would write syntactically wrong ST into the user's repo', while `StAssembler.cs:91-97` invents `END_{kind.ToUpperInvariant()}`. The interface-ordering rule is hand-duplicated verbatim in both. `StSplitter` is documented as the inverse of `PouToStText` and is the sole reader on the push path, so today the tested inverse pair is not the shipped one: a change to child ordering or `%FOLDER` placement in the real emitter keeps both tests green while the real pull→edit→push cycle drops children.
closes: The canonical workspace-ST emit format has two owners — PouToStText ships, StAssembler is what the round-trip tests certify — and the two have already diverged in failure policy
moves.standsAlone: Production code is untouched: `Materializer.cs:20` is the only emitter call site and it calls `PouToStText`. `StAssembler` has exactly two callers, both tests, so the deletion is compiler-checked. No wire bytes, git SHAs or exit codes move. Rewriting the two tests is legitimate under 'tests are the oracle' because their premise — that `StAssembler` is the format under test — is wrong on grounds INDEPENDENT of behaviour: the file has no production caller and says so itself.
moves.gate: dotnet build Volt.Cli.sln -c Release + all three suites, with both repointed tests green.
moves.riskiestPart: The repointed tests may go RED, and that is the whole point: it would mean the shipped emitter and the certified one differ on a case the tests cover. If that happens the move STOPS — the divergence lands as its own named fix move first, and the deletion waits behind it. Do not adjust the tests to stay green.

objections: [mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Watch the one thing the proposed gate is blind to: whether the rewritten arrange blocks actually feed the new emitter the same inputs. Both tests assert only substrings, so a mis-transcribed PouData still passes. The narrower safe form is a two-commit split. Commit 1 (pure, no deletion): add ONE test to Volt.Engine.Tests asserting `Assert.Equal(StAssembler.Assemble(dict), PouToStText.Convert(pou))` for both fixtures — an executable proof of the byte-identity I could only establish by reading, and the red-first signal the author asked for. Whichever form is used, the repointed tests must gain a golden-string assertion (Assert.Equal on the full emitted text) rather than keeping Assert.Contains — otherwise the round-trip pair certifies strictly less after the move than before, which is a coverage regression hiding inside a `shape` move. And carry ARCHITECTURE.md:85 plus the three volt-lsp-iec comments in the same commit; add `using Volt.Engine.Workspace;` to both test files or the build stops at CS0103 before any of this matters.

The reap/miss policy — the three-tick hold, the miss counting — is kept in full.
moves.why: `TrayContext.cs:155` is `var (_, reap) = ...`, so the spawn plan has no production consumer at all, and `EnsureWorker` is called for every live pid every tick regardless. `TwincatSupervisorTests` asserts that dead output: break `Reconcile`'s spawn de-dup and the suite goes red for a change that alters nothing; break `EnsureWorker`'s `_workers` de-dup (which is what stops a second worker attaching COM to the same XAE and colliding on the same `volt.bridge.twincat.<pid>` pipe) and nothing anywhere notices. Deleting the output deletes the false signal; move 24 makes the real rule testable.
closes: TwincatSupervisorTests asserts on a spawn list production discards, while the de-duplication that actually runs lives in the untestable WinForms assembly
moves.standsAlone: `Reconcile(...).Spawn` and `SpawnedPids` have consumers only in `TwincatSupervisorTests`. `Connector.Core` contains no reflection, `dynamic`, `Activator`, `nameof` or string-keyed dispatch, so static absence IS proof here. objections:
[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The one thing to watch: this move must carry `src/Volt.Cli.Connector/TrayContext.cs` in its file set (`var reap = _twincatSupervisor.Reconcile(pids);` at :155) or it cannot compile — the row as handed to the surgeon is missing the file that breaks. Re-state the test impact honestly in the commit body: not "the test", but 3 of 7 cases deleted outright and the other 4 edited, with `Forget`'s only coverage among the deletions.

The narrower form that would be safe RIGHT NOW, with zero risk and zero deconstruction churn: delete only `SpawnedPids` and `Forget` plus TrayContext.cs:169's call to it — both have verified zero production readers, `Forget` is already a proven no-op, and the tuple (hence every call site and every reap/miss test) stays intact. That is most of the ~20 LOC target.md:84 is claiming, with no `shape` move resting on a mass test edit.

If the full deletion proceeds anyway, sequence it AFTER move 24 (`bridge-supervisor-to-core`), not before. The move's "why" inverts the dependency: relocating BridgeSupervisor into Core is what makes the real fleet policy testable, and it needs no help from move 5 to do it (move 24's own What copies `EnsureWorker`-for-every-pid verbatim). Landing 5 first removes the debounced spawn signal and its tests during the window when nothing yet tests the replacement — and if move 24 slips or is reverted, the tree is left with a supervisor that only reaps, a dead `Forget` still called from the tray, and no test anywhere covering worker de-dup.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — FAILS TO COMPILE. The move's declared file set is two files and omits `packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli.Connector/TrayContext.cs`, which at line 155 does `var (_, reap) = _twincatSupervisor.Reconcile(pids);`. Drop the `Spawn` half and that deconstruction has nothing to bind: FIRST error is TrayContext.cs:155, **CS8129** "No suitable 'Deconstruct' instance or extension method was found for type 'System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<int>', with 2 out parameters and a void return type" (with a companion CS1061 on `Deconstruct`). `Volt.Cli.Connector` is project {847A8C45} in Volt.Cli.sln:22 and ProjectReferences Connector.Core (Volt.Cli.Connector.csproj:23), so the move's own gate — `dotnet build Volt.Cli.sln -c Release` — is red before any suite runs. Consequence: the shipped delta is one extra log line, written from the accept thread with NO ordering against the 'ready' line written from the caller's thread — so the log the finding complains about still contains 'bridge ready', now sometimes AFTER the failure line. Volt.Cli.Transport.csproj has ZERO ProjectReferences; Volt.Engine.csproj:23 references Volt.Cli.Transport and never the reverse; VoltLog is Volt.Engine.Diagnostics.VoltLog. [mechanics] objection: Check 7a — the plan's own named red-first test cannot be written against this version. target.md:287 names `A_bridge_whose_pipe_cannot_be_bound_fails_Start_instead_of_reporting_ready`, asserting Start() THROWS. With the synchronous bind dropped, Start() can never throw; the ctor failure is still caught on the background thread. target.md:289 pre-ruled on exactly this: 'this move drops back to log lines only and must be honestly re-labelled and re-scoped — it does not ship on a test that cannot fail.' The move handed to me is log-lines-only and kept the title.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7b — the substitute gate forces a test-infrastructure edit that is not a mechanical file move. VoltLog is a process-global singleton with no reset; test/Volt.Engine.Tests/TestParallelism.cs:3-6 exists solely for that reason ('Tests that Init it and read the file back can't run concurrently with other classes that also log, so serialize the assembly'). The target puts the new test in test/Volt.Cli.Tests/wire/PipeTransportTests.cs, and Volt.Cli.Tests has NO CollectionBehavior attribute — the repo's only two are Engine.Tests and the connector's LivePipeCollection.cs, which move 1 deletes. moves.title: The three sites that report a DROPPED item log where the log actually is
moves.what: `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44`, `CodesysTypeMap.cs:124` and `BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145` change `Console.Error.WriteLine($"[bridge] …")` to `VoltLog.Warn(…)` with the same text. `DriverBase.cs:51` drops its `Console.Error` half and keeps only `VoltLog.Warn($"degraded: {reason}")`. OLD behaviour: CODESYS.exe is a GUI process with no console attached, so the two CODESYS sites — precisely the ones that report an item being DROPPED from the walk — write to nowhere; `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs` holds nothing, and the same event lands on TwinCAT only because `BridgeSupervisor.cs:65` re-tags the worker's stderr through the connector's separate logger. Every degrade is emitted twice, so a log read shows one transition or two depending on which sink you looked at. NEW behaviour: one channel, one line per event, in the file the debugging doc names. Observed by: an engineer whose POUs are missing from `src/` after a pull and who today has nothing to read.
moves.why: ARCHITECTURE.md's invariant is 'Skipped/errored items are logged, never silently dropped (Diagnostics/VoltLog) with name + reason', and convention 5 is 'one error channel, one log path'. These are the exact sites the invariant covers, and they bypass it — so the two vendors have different diagnosability for the same drop by accident of hosting rather than by design. All three candidates missed this; two of the three judges flagged it independently as certain and nearly free.
closes: A second log channel (Console.Error.WriteLine("[bridge] …")) carries exactly the events the log-invariant covers, into a process that has no console
moves.standsAlone: Depends on move 6 only for the CODESYS host to reach `VoltLog` through Transport (it already reaches it through Engine, so strictly this could land earlier — it is sequenced here so all four logging changes are contiguous and one revert range covers them). Four call-site edits; no signature, no frame, no exit code changes.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Engine.Tests`: `DegradeIsLoggedOnce` — assert `MarkDegraded` produces exactly one VoltLog line and writes nothing to a captured `Console.Error`. Red today (DriverBase double-writes). The two vendor-side sites cannot be pinned offline (no test .csproj references either IDE host) — say so in the commit; their check is the live e2e.
moves.riskiestPart: The TwinCAT worker's stderr is redirected into the connector's log by `BridgeSupervisor`, so moving those lines to VoltLog changes WHICH file a TwinCAT drop appears in (from `connector-*.log` to `twincat-*.log`). That is the intended correction, but anyone with a saved grep or a support runbook pointed at the connector log stops finding them. Note it in the commit.
moves.source: synthesized (no candidate proposed it; nominated by judges 1 and 3)
objections: [mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The narrower form that is safe: make it a `shape`-adjacent ADD, not a substitution. At each of the three sites keep `Console.Error.WriteLine` exactly as-is and ADD `VoltLog.Warn(<same text>)` beside it — which is precisely the pattern `DriverBase.cs:51/57` already uses two files away, so it introduces no second answer and removes no channel whose reach (CODESYS message view; the TwinCAT stderr→`Log.Raw` path at `BridgeSupervisor.cs:65`) the move has not proven is dead. That version has no observable loss, so it needs no red-first test it cannot write, and the `using` additions plus the order-6 namespace question are the entire diff. If the surgeon instead substitutes: (1) pin the level to `Warn`, in writing, NEVER `Debug` — VoltLog's default floor is `Info` (VoltLog.cs:28), and `Debug` silently deletes the TwinCAT drop line that reaches the log today; (2) add `using` for wherever move 6 actually put VoltLog to BOTH CODESYS files before touching line 44 or line 124; (3) do not touch the `try/catch` at CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44 or the two static dedupe sets; (4) decide DriverBase.cs:51/57 in the SAME commit or not at all — leaving it half-done is the defect the move claims to close. The one thing to watch: after this lands, the only proof any of the three lines ever reaches the log is a human reading `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs` during a live session. There is no suite that can see it, and the move should say so out loud instead of listing a gate it cannot meet.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (test edits / red-first) — DECISIVE. The gate is "red-first test asserting the drop reaches VoltLog". No such test can be written. All three drop sites live in projects that NO test project references and CANNOT reference: `test/Volt.Cli.Tests`, `test/Volt.Engine.Tests` and `test/Volt.Cli.Connector.Tests` are all `net8.0` (their csprojs, line 3) and reference only Volt.Engine / Volt.Cli.Transport / Volt.Cli / Volt.Cli.Connector.Core. `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys.csproj` is `net48`; `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat.csproj` is `net8.0-windows` Exe. Adding a ProjectReference from any of the three suites yields NU1201 ("Project X is not compatible with net8.0"), in BOTH directions. target.md line 672 concedes this in its own words for a different move: "no test .csproj references Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys" — and that move solved it by MOVING the logic into Core. This move moves nothing; it swaps a writer in place. Consequence: the move ships with no red-first test, i.e. it ships as an untested `fix`, violating its own stated gate and the repo's fix contract.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7, second blocker — even with a reference, the three sites are unreachable from a test. `CodesysTypeMap` is `internal static` and `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys` grants no InternalsVisibleTo; `WarnUnrecognized` (CodesysTypeMap.cs:115) and `WarnUnmappedTcCode` (BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:140) are `private static`; `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44` needs a live CODESYS object model and `BeckhoffDriver` needs a live COM XAE attach. Worse for testability: both warn helpers dedupe through process-wide statics (`_loggedUnknown` CodesysTypeMap.cs:111, `_loggedTcCodes` BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:137) with no reset, so a second test in the same process observes NOTHING — the assertion is order-dependent by construction.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — fails twice. (a) Applied to the tree as it stands today it does not compile (see reasoning: CS0103). (b) It is sequenced at order 8, AFTER order 6 `voltlog-down-to-transport`, which relocates VoltLog out of `Volt.Engine.Diagnostics` into Transport. The move text names no namespace and its `files` field names `packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Engine/` — the directory VoltLog will have LEFT by the time this move runs. The correct `using` is therefore unknown from the move as written and differs depending on whether move 6 has landed. Consequence: a surgeon guesses the namespace, or the commit does not build in either ordering.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (observable delta must be NAMED) — the stated premise is factually false for one of the three sites, and the real delta is unnamed. `BridgeSupervisor.cs:65-66` already pipes the TwinCAT worker's stderr into the durable store: `proc.ErrorDataReceived += (_, e) => Log.Raw(w.Id, e.Data)`, and `Connector.Core/Log.Raw` writes to the SAME `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs\twincat-<date>.log`. So BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145 does NOT "go nowhere" — it lands in the log today. What actually changes there is the line SHAPE (`[ts][twincat] [bridge] unmapped TwinCAT TREEITEMTYPE …` → `[ts][twincat][warn] …`), which the move never names. And the move never names the LEVEL: the nearest neighbour for exactly this event class, `FetchService.cs:79`, logs drops at `VoltLog.Debug` ("fetch skip: unmapped-kind"). If the surgeon matches that neighbour, VoltLog's default `Info` floor (VoltLog.cs:28) makes the TwinCAT drop VANISH from the default log — a net loss of diagnosability on the vendor the move claims to be levelling up. An unspecified level in a move whose whole content is "which sink and how loud" is an unnamed behaviour delta.

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (Conventions — one answer to one question) — the move as handed to me touches only the three drop sites, leaving `DriverBase.cs:51` and `:57` dual-writing Console.Error AND VoltLog for the degraded transitions. After this commit the codebase has TWO answers to "how does the bridge report an anomaly": dual-write at DriverBase, VoltLog-only at the three drop sites. target.md line 296 says the DriverBase Console.Error half is also dropped, and lists DriverBase.cs in its `Files.` line — but the move row I was given says "the three sites" and its `files` field is `src/Volt.Engine/`, which contains ZERO of those three sites and only DriverBase. The move is internally contradictory about its own scope: three-sites-in-Engine describes nothing that exists.

[invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The objection to carry: this is not a three-line substitution, it is a change to what the CONNECTOR's log window shows, and the move as written neither names that nor tests it. Insist on three things before it lands. (1) Name the level explicitly — `VoltLog.Warn` at all three sites — and in the same commit lift BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:36/40/42 out of `Debug`, or state in the commit why the sibling walk guards stay Debug; otherwise the move manufactures the exact cross-vendor asymmetry it was written to remove. (2) Do DriverBase.cs:51/57 in the same commit — drop its `Console.Error` half — because leaving it is leaving the second log channel open in the one directory the move actually declares, and the finding is not closed without it. (3) Name the connector delta in the commit message: the TwinCAT drop line moves from Source=`twincat.<pid>` / Level=blank / file `twincat.<pid>-*.log` to Source=`twincat` / Level=`warn` / file `twincat-*.log`, and the `[bridge]` prefix disappears — a user with the LogWindow source filter pinned per-instance loses the line. The narrower form that would be safe TODAY: take only `CodesysTypeMap.cs:124` and `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44` at `VoltLog.Warn` (the two where the GUI in-proc host genuinely has no sink), leave `BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145` on `Console.Error` until the connector-log delta is decided, and gate it by a manual headless run (`codesys-pipe.ps1 up` → walk → assert the line in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs\codesys-*.log`) — since no automated suite can reach either host project, an honest manual gate is better than a green one that ran nothing.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 — observable change is REAL but UNNAMED, and lands in a component the move never declares. The TwinCAT site is not "going nowhere": BridgeSupervisor.cs:65-66 attaches `proc.ErrorDataReceived += (_, e) => Log.Raw(w.Id, e.Data)` to the worker, and TrayContext.cs:162 sets `TwincatWorkerId(pid) => $"{Vendors.Twincat}.{pid}"`. So today BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145 lands in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs\twincat.<pid>-<date>.log` with Source=`twincat.12345`, Level=BLANK. After the move it lands in `twincat-<date>.log` with Source=`twincat`, Level=`warn`, and without the `[bridge]` prefix. LogWindow.cs:24-26 PARSES exactly this shape (`^\[ts\]\[src\](\[lvl\])?\s?msg$`, with the comment "level optional — worker Raw lines have none") and LogWindow.cs:107-114 FILTERS on Src and Lvl. Consequence: an operator with the LogWindow source dropdown pinned to `twincat.<pid>` — the only per-instance source there is — stops seeing dropped-item warnings entirely, and the row's Source/Level/Message columns all change value. That is "a log line another component parses", changed silently.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 (second, undeclared surface) — codesys-pipe.ps1:39/99 redirects the headless CODESYS host's stderr to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\volt-bridge\codesys-pipe-err.log`. The two CODESYS `[bridge]` drop lines DO go somewhere in the prescribed headless dev/test loop today. Consequence: the move relocates them out of the err log an engineer following CLAUDE.md's documented loop is tailing, and the move's stated premise ("a GUI process with no console — they go nowhere") is false for both the headless CODESYS loop and for TwinCAT.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 / scope — the declared `files:` is `packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Engine/`. ZERO of the three sites are in Volt.Engine. They are in `src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys/Driver/CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44`, `src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys/Ide/CodesysTypeMap.cs:124`, and `src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat/Driver/BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145` — i.e. entirely inside the two vendor host projects, the vendor seam. Consequence: the move cannot be reviewed against its own declared blast radius, and it is scoped as an Engine change when it is a two-driver change.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — the move does NOT close the finding it claims to close, and splits the channel it claims to unify. findings.md:707 lists FOUR sites and its "Smallest fix" (findings.md:721) is explicitly two-part: "Those three sites should call VoltLog.Warn; DriverBase should drop its Console.Error half." The move does part one only. After it, DriverBase.cs:51 and :57 still write `[bridge] DEGRADED` / `[bridge] DEGRADED cleared` to Console.Error alongside VoltLog. Consequence: the "second log channel" the move exists to remove is still open, in Volt.Engine, which is the one directory the move actually names.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — the move names no LEVEL, which is the whole behavior delta. VoltLog.cs:28 defaults `_level = VoltLogLevel.Info`, so `VoltLog.Debug` is SILENT by default. BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:36/40/42 already log the analogous per-node walk guards at `VoltLog.Debug`, while CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44's guard (whose own comment says "matches Beckhoff") would become Warn if the mover picks Warn. Consequence: "replace with VoltLog calls" resolves either to Warn (a new Warn-vs-Debug split for the same class of walk-guard event across the two drivers — a NEW cross-vendor diagnosability asymmetry created by the move that claims to remove one) or to Debug (all three lines vanish from the default log, a strictly worse outcome than today). An unnamed level is an unnamed behavior delta.

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first gate CANNOT be written in any of the three suites. Every test project is `net8.0`: Volt.Engine.Tests, Volt.Cli.Tests, Volt.Cli.Connector.Tests. None of them ProjectReferences `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys` (`net48`) or `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat` (`net8.0-windows`), and neither reference is even legal from a `net8.0` project (net8.0 does not satisfy net48; net8.0 does not satisfy net8.0-windows → NU1201). Consequence: "red-first test asserting the drop reaches VoltLog" requires a new test project or a multi-target retarget that the move does not declare and that is not a mechanical file move.

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — the author's stated riskiest part is factually false. I grepped the whole `packages/volt-cli` tree for `Console.SetError`, `StringWriter`, and each of the three message strings: NO test captures Console.Error, and no test references these strings at all. Consequence: the one risk the author modeled does not exist, while the two that do (the connector LogWindow parse/filter surface and the untestable gate) went unmodeled. A move whose only stated risk is imaginary has not been reasoned about.

[invariants] objection: Check 8 — "all three suites pass" is vacuously true and proves nothing. No suite compiles or loads either edited project, so the gate has ZERO coverage of the change. The build does succeed (statement-body substitution only), which is exactly what makes the empty gate dangerous: it will report green regardless of whether the level, the prefix, or the connector's Source column were got right.

(1) Correct `files` to the two files in `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys` and one in `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat`, and state explicitly whether `DriverBase.cs:51,57` is in or out — `target.md:296` and `findings.md:715` say in, the card says nothing, and that file is in a different project and on the health path. (3) Leave `BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:145` ALONE in this move — its line is already durable via `BridgeSupervisor.cs:66`, so the change there is a pure relocation across log files and source tags with zero diagnosability gain, and it is the one site whose premise the move states incorrectly. (4) If the substitution (rather than dual-write) is genuinely wanted, that is a separate, argued decision about `DriverBase`'s dual-sink convention and should be its own move with `DriverBase` as the subject. THE ONE THING TO WATCH: the `try { … } catch (Exception ex) { …; return; }` at `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:41-44` is the CODESYS mirror of Beckhoff's per-node catch. moves.title: One logger, one directory — the connector stops running its own copy
moves.what: Delete `Volt.Cli.Connector.Core/Log.cs` (49) and repoint its ~40 call sites (`ConnectionManager` ×12, `ControlServer`, `BridgeSupervisor`, `LogWindow`, `Pruner`, `TrayContext`, `Updater`) at `VoltLog`; call `VoltLog.Init("connector")` once in `Volt.Cli.Connector/Program.cs` beside the existing startup work. OLD behaviour: connector lines are always written at one verbosity and `connector-*.log` is never pruned. NEW behaviour: connector lines obey `VOLT_LOG_DEBUG=1` (Debug lines appear when set, suppressed when not) and the shared 14-day `Prune()` runs at connector start. The emitted `[ts][source][level] msg` grammar is unchanged, so `LogWindow`'s regex reader keeps parsing. Observed by: anyone troubleshooting with the documented `VOLT_LOG_DEBUG` switch, and any machine that runs the tray but never activates a bridge (its logs stop growing without bound).
moves.why: Two hand-retyped writers into one directory, and the copy has already dropped the level gate and the retention policy the original documents — so ARCHITECTURE.md's 'daily files pruned after 14 days' is FALSE for the one always-on writer, and the documented troubleshooting switch does nothing for the half of the system that owns sessions, leases and reconcile. That is the exact component a user is troubleshooting when they report 'it says connected but push is refused'.
closes: Volt.Cli.Connector.Core/Log.cs re-implements VoltLog by hand, and the copy has already dropped the level gate and the retention policy the original documents
moves.standsAlone: Depends on move 6 — `Connector.Core` already references `Volt.Cli.Transport`, so no new reference is added and the deliberate non-reference to `Volt.Engine` is untouched. The line format is identical so no log consumer notices.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Cli.Connector.Tests`: `Connector_debug_lines_are_suppressed_without_VOLT_LOG_DEBUG` — red today, because `Log.cs` has no level concept at all.
moves.riskiestPart: `VoltLog.Prune()` DELETES every `*.log` older than 14 days in a directory shared with installer logs (`install-*`, `uninstall-*`, which `LogWindow` deliberately skips). The connector is the always-on process, so prune now runs on machines where it never ran — an engineer who kept old logs for a support ticket loses them on the next tray start. Confirm `Prune`'s glob before landing; if it is not already source-scoped, scope it. Second: `ConnectionManager` unit tests currently do real file I/O through `Log`'s process-wide lock — confirm `Init`-from-tests does not start writing to the developer's real store.
moves.source: minimal-move + seam-first + delete-first (all three, identically)
objections: [invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Do not ship the level-gate claim without the demotion that makes it real. The narrower form that is safe, and that I would not object to: split this into (i) a pure SHAPE move that deletes Log.cs, repoints all ~40 call sites — including Updater.cs and Pruner.cs — at VoltLog, and places `VoltLog.Init("connector")` as the FIRST statement of Program.cs.Main, above the `--uninstall` branch, so no line that is written today is lost; assert byte-identical output and drop the red-first test, because there is none to write. Then (ii) a separate, genuinely red-first FIX move that scopes `VoltLog.Prune()` to the process's own source prefix — named as the behaviour change it is, with a test that installer logs survive a prune, since LogWindow.cs:168-177 and scripts/test-install.ts:182-192 both depend on those files existing. Then (iii), if wanted at all, a third fix that demotes named connector Info lines to Debug — that one CAN be red-first and IS the level gate paying for itself. If it proceeds as one move anyway, the single thing to watch is `VoltLog.Init` placement: every log line emitted before it (Pruner, VoltEnv, the uninstall hook, ControlServer inside the ControlHarness) silently becomes nothing, and unlike today's writer there is no output to notice its absence in.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 (observable delta must be NAMED) — the move's headline NEW behaviour, "connector lines obey VOLT_LOG_DEBUG=1 (Debug lines appear when set, suppressed when not)", is vacuous: Log.cs declares Info/Warn/Error/Raw and NO Debug (Log.cs:17-25), and the move's "What" repoints call sites without demoting any. Zero connector call sites are Debug before or after, so setting VOLT_LOG_DEBUG changes not one connector line. The only way to make the gate observable is to demote existing Info lines to Debug — an unnamed change to which lines connector-*.log and LogWindow contain, in exactly the component the move says a user is troubleshooting.

Editing test/shared/FakeIde.cs is therefore discretionary surgery on the exact double ARCHITECTURE.md convention 10 names as the one that hid a real bug — including StaleHealthSnapshot (FakeIde.cs:106-108, 239-241), the knob that makes the TwinCAT cached-vs-live divergence representable.

So either this move depends on 12 and does not stand alone, or 12 has not landed and the FakeIde edit is unnecessary. The plan itself has not settled it: target.md:15/135-136/397 put the fake at 12 BEFORE health at 13, target.md:830 says the fake 'must land BEFORE any of the three', but target.md:791 says 'health-compose-in-core lands next, ALONE ... and fake-ide-derives-driverbase FOLLOWS'. An unresolved prerequisite is not a stand-alone move.

[invariants] objection: Check 8 (gate is hollow) — I grepped every test/*/*.csproj: NONE references Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys or Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat. 'build + 3 suites' cannot execute one line of either rewritten driver; HonestHealthTests.cs only calls the static DriverBase.DeriveServedStatus. target.md:720 concedes this. The only real gate is the two-vendor live e2e, which target.md:720 and :791 make a hard precondition ('if the live e2e cannot be run on both vendors in the same session, THIS MOVE DOES NOT LAND') — and I could not verify that a two-vendor session is available.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 (conventions 8) — the card drops the PipeHost.cs correction. target.md:651 and :695 assign the false-comment fix to THIS move ('corrected inside health-compose-in-core'), and the false comment is live: PipeHost.cs (Stop) says `_driver?.Disconnect(); // drop change-event handlers from the singleton ObjectManager` while CodesysDriver.cs:45 is `public override void Disconnect() { ClearDegraded(); }` and nothing registers handlers. The card's files list omits both PipeHost.cs and IIdeSession.cs, so a convention-8 defect the plan says this move closes goes unclosed.

[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The objection to carry: "the fake's switch to SnapshotHealth" is the whole move, not an afterthought — DriverBase's composition is CACHE-then-async-probe, FakeIde's is a pure function of live `init` knobs evaluated at call time, and nothing seeds a fake's cache because no fake has a Connect(). Split it. A narrower form that could be safe: FIRST land a move that gives IIdeDriver/DriverBase an explicit, vendor-agnostic startup seed (the thing CodesysDriver.Connect and BeckhoffDriver.Connect already do informally, which BridgePipeHost never calls), and have FakeIde seed through it after its initializers run — then this move becomes genuinely mechanical. Failing that, keep FakeIde's BuildHealthResponse override (it is a `virtual`, not `abstract`, on the new base) so the fake's live-knob semantics survive, and accept that the fake still does not exercise the new composition — which is honest, and much cheaper than editing ten test files. Whoever writes it: use `unchecked(Environment.TickCount - stamp)` widened to long with an explicit `_everStamped` bool, never `TickCount64` and never `== 0` as the sentinel; and publish `_hasProject` BEFORE PublishRows in CodesysDriver.SnapshotHealth, with a comment saying why.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — HARD FAIL, deterministic. After this commit and nothing else, Volt.Cli.Tests goes red. DriverBase's new BuildHealthResponse serves a cache published only by the ASYNC probe, but nothing ever seeds FakeIde's cache: BridgePipeHost's ctor/Start (src/Volt.Engine/Wire/BridgePipeHost.cs:29-34) call no Connect, and unlike CodesysDriver.Connect (CodesysDriver.cs:44) and BeckhoffDriver.Connect (BeckhoffDriver.cs:41) — the two production seeds — FakeIde has none. So the FIRST `health` returns an empty projects array. test/Volt.Cli.Tests/wire/PipeTransportTests.cs:238 `Health_poll_answers_from_cache_while_the_one_IDE_thread_is_busy_with_a_long_op` fails NON-RACILY: the fake is `serializeSta: true` with the STA thread held inside `init`, so the kicked probe (RunProbeOnce -> Task.Run -> RunOnStaThread -> the blocked queue) cannot publish, and `Assert.True(... arr.GetArrayLength() == 1, "health did not carry the connectable-projects list")` fails. That is the exact test ARCHITECTURE.md:59 names as the guard for the health-must-not-marshal invariant.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (test edits) — HARD STOP for a shape move. Fixing the above requires editing tests or redesigning FakeIde, not a mechanical file move. The obvious repair (seed the cache in FakeIde's ctor) is structurally impossible: every health knob is an object-initializer property assigned AFTER the ctor runs — `HealthConnected {get;init;}` (FakeIde.cs:97), `HealthProjectName {get;init;}` (:105), `StaleHealthSnapshot {get;init;}` (:108), `Projects {get;set;}` (:260) — so a ctor-time SnapshotHealth caches the DEFAULTS, and every call site that sets them (CodesysMultiInstanceTests.cs:25-32, PipeTransportTests.cs:82/125/130/249, CommandHarness.cs:31, BlackBoxTests.cs:146/162, InitCommandTests.cs:87, StatusCommandTests.cs:55, PullCommandTests.cs:181, OpGuardTests.cs:19/65) gets wrong rows. The only other repair — make the cold-cache probe synchronous — marshals `health` onto the IDE thread on the first poll, i.e. re-creates the regression the guard exists for. The move calls this change 'compiler-forced, mechanical'; it is neither.

[mechanics] objection: Check 6 (netstandard2.0) — the move hoists TwinCAT's throttle clock into Volt.Engine (netstandard2.0, src/Volt.Engine/Volt.Engine.csproj:5). BeckhoffDriver's ONLY clock expressions are `Environment.TickCount64` (BeckhoffDriver.cs:57 and :88). TickCount64 does not exist in netstandard2.0 — DriverBase.cs:184 says so in its own comment, and map.md:82 lists it as a named consequence of the target framework.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (nothing observable changes) — two unnamed deltas. (a) Re-basing TwinCAT's throttle onto 32-bit `Environment.TickCount`: the `_cachedAtMs == 0 ? null : ...` never-probed sentinel becomes ambiguous, and a non-`unchecked` age subtraction goes hugely negative after the ~24.9-day wrap, so `age > 5000` stays false and the TwinCAT probe STOPS FIRING for up to 24.9 days on a long-running worker — health freezes on a live PLC, silently. (b) CODESYS with `ProbeThrottleMs => 0` gets `if (age is null || age > 0)`; `Environment.TickCount` has ~15.6 ms granularity, so two polls landing in one tick (routine: tray + VS Code panel + desktop all poll) now SKIP a probe CodesysDriver.cs:95 fires unconditionally today. Neither is named.

moves.title: CODESYS gets the same health-probe throttle TwinCAT has
moves.what: Delete `BeckhoffDriver`'s `ProbeThrottleMs` override and change `DriverBase.ProbeThrottleMs` from a `virtual` returning 0 to a single `const`. OLD behaviour: CODESYS marshals `SnapshotHealth` (HasPrimaryProject / HasObjectManager / ProjectName / ProjectDirty over the reflection object model) onto the engineer's IDE PRIMARY thread on EVERY health poll — the tray polls ~4s per pipe, plus every control-plane `/status`, plus every volt-control `refreshHealth()` — while TwinCAT does one per 5s. NEW behaviour: at most one probe per interval on both vendors. Observed by: a CODESYS engineer with the tray plus a VS Code panel plus the desktop window open, whose IDE thread stops taking back-to-back object-model reads for as long as any Volt frontend is running.
moves.why: 'Any per-vendor difference that Volt can OBSERVE is a bug', and this one has real cost on the user's own IDE thread. Nobody chose the asymmetry; it existed because the throttle lived in the copy. Landing it as a separate fix is what lets move 13 be behaviour-preserving.
closes: DriverBase.BuildHealthResponse is abstract, so the health-poll throttle is a per-vendor decision — CODESYS fires an IDE-thread probe on every single poll, TwinCAT one per 5s (behavioural half)
moves.standsAlone: Depends on moves 12 and 13. Given those, it is a one-line change plus its test; the wire SHAPE is untouched.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Engine.Tests`: `N_health_polls_inside_one_throttle_window_trigger_exactly_one_probe` over the DriverBase-derived fake with a probe counter. Red today for a 0-interval driver. PLUS re-read the e2e's `ide-restart` timing assumptions before landing.
moves.riskiestPart: Choosing the interval — and it is the one genuinely open decision in this plan (see openQuestions). CODESYS's `SelectProject` calls `SnapshotHealth` directly, so a rebind still shows at once, but a project OPENED in the IDE with no select now takes up to the interval to appear in the tray. That is within the connector's own 4s poll jitter at 5000ms, but it is the one user-visible consequence, and CODESYS's snapshot is much cheaper than TwinCAT's STA round-trip so the honest number may be smaller.

objections: [mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Carry this objection: on CODESYS the probe is not just the health-row refresher, it is the sole writer of the op-guard precondition. The one thing to watch is `volt pull`/`volt push` issued in the seconds after a project is opened or reopened in CODESYS — today that recovers within one 2-4s poll, after this it can return PLC_DISCONNECTED for ~8s (5000ms throttle aliased against the 4000ms tray poll), and if the project is CLOSED in that window the guard stays wrongly true and the write proceeds against a dead object model. The narrower form that would be safe: split the cheap liveness read from the row snapshot — keep `_hasProject`/`HasPrimaryProject` refreshed on every poll (it is four reflection reads of top-level state, and `SingleFlight` at DriverBase.cs:139 already bounds it to one concurrent probe) and throttle only the row composition. Or land the throttle only after `CodesysDriver.IsConnected` stops reading a probe-written cache, which is a different move. Also fix the row before applying it: `files` must include `BeckhoffDriver.cs` and `HonestHealthTests.cs`, the const must be at least `internal` (Volt.Engine already has `InternalsVisibleTo("Volt.Engine.Tests")`) so the test does not re-spell 5000, and the red-first test needs an injected clock — it cannot be made red by polling in a loop.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone / compiles as written) — the move's `files` list is ONE file, `src/Volt.Engine/Ide/DriverBase.cs`, but its own `what` requires deleting `BeckhoffDriver.ProbeThrottleMs`. Applied exactly as written, `Volt.Engine` (netstandard2.0) compiles clean and then `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat` fails: **CS0115 'BeckhoffDriver.ProbeThrottleMs': no suitable method found to override** — a `const` field cannot be overridden by `protected override long ProbeThrottleMs => 5000;`. Both IDE projects are in `Volt.Cli.sln` (lines 16 and 18), so `dotnet build Volt.Cli.sln -c Release` — the move's own gate — fails on step one.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (the behaviour delta must be NAMED) — the move names exactly one observable: 'what the tray shows within a 5s window'. It produces a second, unnamed one on the WRITE path. `CodesysDriver.IsConnected` (CodesysDriver.cs:36) reads the cached `_hasProject`, and `SnapshotHealth` (CodesysDriver.cs:61) is its ONLY ambient writer — the probe. `OpGuard.RequireBoundProject` (OpGuard.cs:27) and `RefsService` (RefsService.cs:21) throw `PLC_DISCONNECTED` off that exact signal. Throttling the probe therefore throttles the precondition for every `refs`/`fetch`/`push`/`build`, on CODESYS only. The driver's own comment (CodesysDriver.cs:35) says the reopen path recovers 'on its own: the live PrimaryProject lookup makes the next probe flip `_hasProject` back' — this move lengthens exactly that window.

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (ARCHITECTURE.md §Conventions #3, 'One question, one answer') — convention 3 is written verbatim against this: 'The not-connected precondition is decided from live driver state (`IIdeSession.IsConnected` + `ServedProjectName`), never from `BuildHealthResponse()` — health is served from a per-vendor **throttled cache**, and deciding a write against it refused pushes on stale state while reads of the same bridge succeeded.' The move does not read `BuildHealthResponse()` from the guard, but it achieves the same thing by putting CODESYS's `IsConnected` behind the same throttle. The convention exists because that failure already shipped once.

[mechanics] objection: Check 2 (load-bearing asymmetry) — the cadence divergence is NOT the arbitrary copy-paste artefact the move claims ('nobody chose the asymmetry'). It tracks the hosting-model asymmetry ARCHITECTURE.md marks irreducible. `BeckhoffDriver.IsConnected` is `_om.IsConnected` = `_dte != null && _sysManager != null` (TcObjectModel.cs:47) — plain fields, NOT written by the snapshot, so throttling the snapshot cannot touch the op precondition. `CodesysDriver.IsConnected` IS the snapshot. TwinCAT can afford a 5s throttle for a structural reason CODESYS does not share; unifying the number unifies two things that are not the same thing.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (the red-first test must actually be red first) — `N_health_polls_inside_one_throttle_window_trigger_exactly_one_probe` is not reliably red before the fix, for two independent reasons already in the tree. (a) `DriverBase.SingleFlight` (DriverBase.cs:139-158) drops any probe raised while one is in flight, so N rapid polls already coalesce to 1 at ANY throttle. (b) After move 13 the guard is `age is null || age > ProbeThrottleMs`; with `ProbeThrottleMs == 0` and `Environment.TickCount` granularity (~15.6ms on Windows) a tight poll loop sees `age == 0`, which is not `> 0`, so no probe fires. A green pre-fix test is the failure mode; making it deterministically red needs sleeps or an injected clock the move does not specify. Separately, 'a single `const`' as written is private, so the test in `Volt.Engine.Tests` cannot read it and must hardcode 5000 — a constant re-spelt outside its home file (convention 7).

[invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: The objection to carry: do not delete the seam. `health-compose-in-core` introduces `protected virtual long ProbeThrottleMs`; the safe form of this fix is to give CODESYS a SMALL non-zero override (~1000ms — below the connector's ~4s poll, so `_hasProject` never goes staler than it does today) and leave TwinCAT's 5000 untouched. That bounds the in-proc IDE-thread load, which is the whole stated benefit, without coupling a 4-property in-proc reflection read to a cross-process DTE round-trip and without widening the OpGuard/BridgeResolver staleness window. Deleting the override to force one `const` is the part that fails checks 2 and 4, and it buys nothing observable. If it proceeds anyway: (a) name the second and third deltas in the commit — `volt pull/push/build` PLC_DISCONNECTED after an IDE-side project open, and BridgeResolver's PLC_DISCONNECTED/AMBIGUOUS_BRIDGE pipe-choice window — because they are the ones on the live-PLC path, not the tray; (b) make the red-first test defeat `SingleFlight` by joining each background probe before the next poll, or it is green before the fix and proves nothing; (c) do not hoist `Environment.TickCount64` into `Volt.Engine` — it is not on netstandard2.0 (DriverBase.cs:184 says so), and the int-`TickCount` substitute needs an explicit never-snapshotted flag rather than a `0` sentinel; (d) re-check the ~500-test suite for assertions that flip when the shared fake becomes throttled — per the plan's own rule, an assertion that has to change is the finding, not the fix.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 — the behavior delta is REAL but MIS-NAMED. The move names one consequence ("what the tray shows within a 5s window"). The actual observable set is larger and sits on the data-safety path. CodesysDriver.cs:36 `IsConnected => _dispatcher != null && _hasProject && _om.HasObjectManager`, and `_hasProject` is written ONLY by `SnapshotHealth` (CodesysDriver.cs:53-63), whose only ambient caller is the probe (:101). OpGuard.cs:27 throws PLC_DISCONNECTED off that live-but-probe-fed signal for fetch/push/build. Throttling the probe therefore widens the window in which `volt pull/push/build` refuse with a nonzero exit code and a PLC_DISCONNECTED stderr line after the engineer opens/reopens a project in CODESYS — from ~one poll (sub-second with tray + VS Code + desktop all polling) to a deterministic ~interval. CodesysDriver.cs:56-58 documents this EXACT failure as a shipped bug once already: "reporting serving=false for ~4s after Connect and bouncing a pull/push with PLC_DISCONNECTED". An unnamed delta on the CLI exit-code surface is, by the brief's own rule, the same defect as a shape move that moves behavior.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 (second, sharper) — BridgeResolver picks WHICH IDE the CLI writes to from the THROTTLED health cache. BridgeResolver.cs:64 `new BridgeClient(pipe).GetHealth().Projects.Select(p => p.Project)` feeds ChooseBridgePipe (:53-59). With two CODESYS open, a bound project just opened in window B is absent from B's cached rows for up to the interval → `matches.Count == 0` → PLC_DISCONNECTED "isn't open in any of the 2 running CODESYS"; a project just MOVED between windows leaves both rows listing it → AMBIGUOUS_BRIDGE "close all but one". Both are new CLI-visible refusals, and they now REPEAT on an immediate retry: today the CLI's own health call kicks a probe so the next call sees fresh rows; under a throttle the retry answers from the same stale cache. Neither is named.

[invariants] objection: Check 2 — this unifies a policy that exists BECAUSE of the first load-bearing asymmetry. ARCHITECTURE.md:153-155: CODESYS = in-proc net48 reflection; Beckhoff = net8 exe over cross-process COM. BeckhoffDriver.cs:74-77 states the throttle's purpose in those terms ("a user who isn't syncing never has Volt slow or crash their IDE") for a snapshot that does EnsureAttached + ProbeIdeAlive + OwnSolution over RPC; CodesysDriver.cs:51-52 says its own snapshot is "Cheap here (the one in-proc primary project) … on TwinCAT the same snapshot carries the heavier ROT walk". One `const` cannot be right for both, and the plan ADMITS the number is unchosen (target.md:718 — "the honest shared number may be smaller. Decide the number before the move lands"). The brief handed to me states no value. If it lands below 5000 the move silently TIGHTENS TwinCAT's cross-process COM cadence on the engineer's XAE — a regression on the vendor the throttle was written for, caused by a fix whose stated purpose is protecting the IDE thread. A fix move whose entire content is one constant cannot be judged when the constant is undecided.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — convention 3 ("one question, one answer", ARCHITECTURE.md and OpGuard.cs:18-23). Two paths already answer "is the bound project reachable": OpGuard from LIVE `IsConnected`/`ServedProjectName`, BridgeResolver from the THROTTLED health cache. The convention text names precisely this split as the bug that "refused pushes with PLC_DISCONNECTED on stale state while reads of the same bridge succeeded". On CODESYS today the divergence is small because one per-poll probe feeds both. The move widens it on the only vendor where it was narrow, without touching either consumer. Convention 6 also applies literally: "do not unify those for symmetry."

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first test can be GREEN before the fix, for the wrong reason. `RunProbeOnce` (DriverBase.cs:124) routes through `SingleFlight` (:139-158), which DROPS any probe requested while one is in flight. A test that fires N health polls in a tight loop against a 0-interval driver already collapses them to one probe — so `N_health_polls_inside_one_throttle_window_trigger_exactly_one_probe` passes today unless it forces each background `Task.Run` probe to COMPLETE between polls. The gate does not acknowledge this. Worse, the test can only run against FakeIde: target.md:720 records that NO C# test constructs either driver (no test .csproj references either IDE-host assembly), so nothing offline proves the claim about CODESYS's primary thread, and no e2e test counts probes either — the "live CODESYS e2e" in the gate can only confirm nothing broke.

[invariants] objection: Check 8 — as briefed it does not compile, and it does not stand alone. The brief lists ONE file (DriverBase.cs); target.md:14 lists three (DriverBase.cs, BeckhoffDriver.cs, HonestHealthTests.cs). Turning `virtual ProbeThrottleMs` into a `const` while BeckhoffDriver still carries `override … => 5000` is a hard compile error, so the one-file version fails `dotnet build`. It also depends on moves 12 AND 13, and 13's own gate (target.md:720, :791) says it "DOES NOT LAND" without a live e2e on BOTH vendors in one session — which the plan flags as unconfirmed. "Stands alone" is stated in the brief as "Depends on health-compose-in-core (order 13)", which is the opposite of standing alone.

[hidden] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Carry this objection: on CODESYS the probe is not just the health refresher, it is the ONLY writer of `_hasProject` — the bool `OpGuard` (OpGuard.cs:27), `BridgePipeHost`'s connect post-condition (BridgePipeHost.cs:92) and `GuardEmptyItems` (BridgeClient.cs:61-68) all decide against. Do not land the throttle until that coupling is severed, and do not accept "the tray is staler" as the named delta. The narrower safe form, in order: (1) first make CODESYS's connectedness a genuinely live read on the marshalled thread (every reader I found — OpGuard, RefsService.cs:21, BridgePipeHost.cs:92, PipeHost.cs:81 — already runs on the primary thread, so the "read off-thread" justification at CodesysDriver.cs:25 may itself be stale; verify that before relying on it), so OpGuard's documented "LIVE, not the throttled cache" rule becomes true on both vendors; (2) only then throttle, and throttle ROW COMPOSITION only; (3) pick the number against the connector's actual poll, not against TwinCAT — 5000ms against a ~4s poll aliases to an ~8s refresh, so if 5000 is kept the commit must say "up to ~8s", and the red-first test must assert the observed staleness of `IsConnected`, not the probe count. If (1) is out of scope, the honest minimum is a throttle strictly below the fastest client poll (so no aliasing) plus a forced `SnapshotHealth` whenever the cached gate says not-connected — a refusal must never be decided on a throttled cache.

[hidden] objection: Check 5 (my primary lens) — PASSES on the literal question, and I say so rather than manufacturing a hit: nothing this move touches is reachable without a compile-time reference. But the search turned up the hidden edge that DOES sink it: on CODESYS the health probe is the ONLY writer of `_hasProject` (CodesysDriver.cs:25,53-63), and `_hasProject` is what `IsConnected` (CodesysDriver.cs:36) is made of — so throttling the probe throttles the WRITE GATE, not just the tray. That path has no compile-time link to the throttle at all: DriverBase's throttle constant and OpGuard.cs:27 never mention each other.

[hidden] objection: Check 1 — the observable delta is under-named. The move names one (`the tray shows staler health within a 5s window`). The real set on CODESYS also includes: (a) WHEN `PLC_DISCONNECTED` is raised for refs/fetch/init/push/build (OpGuard.cs:27 → CodesysDriver.cs:36 → `_hasProject`); (b) `HealthResponse.Connected` as read by `BridgeClient.GuardEmptyItems` (BridgeClient.cs:61-68), the guard that stops a zero-item fetch being treated as truth; (c) `BridgeResolver`'s pipe→project match (BridgeResolver.cs:64). An unnamed behaviour delta is the same defect either way, and two of these three are write/data-safety paths, not UI.

[hidden] objection: Check 4 (§Conventions — one question, one answer) — OpGuard.cs:18-23 states the precondition is read from LIVE driver state and 'deliberately does NOT read BuildHealthResponse(): that is served from a per-vendor THROTTLED cache (~5s on TwinCAT), so deciding a write against it refused pushes with PLC_DISCONNECTED on stale state'. On CODESYS the 'live' state IS the probe cache. This move makes the throttled cache the de facto source of the write gate — reintroducing, structurally, the exact coupling that comment forbids in prose. CodesysDriver.cs:56-58 records the same failure already shipped once ('bouncing a pull/push with PLC_DISCONNECTED').

[hidden] objection: Check 2 (load-bearing asymmetry) — the two cadences are not the same quantity, so unifying the NUMBER unifies two different things. TwinCAT's `IsConnected` is a genuinely live field read (`_dte != null && _sysManager != null`, TcObjectModel.cs:47), so its 5s throttle governs health ROWS only. CODESYS's is cache-fed because the in-proc host must answer off the primary thread (CodesysDriver.cs:25). That divergence is downstream of the in-proc-vs-external hosting asymmetry ARCHITECTURE.md marks irreducible; 'nobody chose the asymmetry' (target.md:425) is wrong — the hosting model chose it.

[hidden] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — the move row I was given lists ONE file (DriverBase.cs). target.md:430 lists three. Changing `virtual long ProbeThrottleMs` to a `const` in DriverBase alone leaves `BeckhoffDriver`'s `override` referring to a non-virtual member: the solution does not build. As given, the move cannot stand alone even in the trivial sense.

[hidden] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first test cannot be written against today's tree, and given moves 12+13 it still would not cover what breaks. Today the only test reaching DriverBase is the static `DeriveServedStatus` theory (HonestHealthTests.cs:31); no test constructs a DriverBase-derived driver. And 'N polls in one window trigger exactly one probe' asserts the cadence — not the `_hasProject`/`IsConnected` staleness that is the actual regression surface.

[hidden] objection: Check 6 — passes for THIS move in isolation (a `const long` is netstandard2.0-legal), but the move's entire semantics rest on a clock its dependency has to reimplement: BeckhoffDriver.cs:57,88 uses `Environment.TickCount64`, unavailable in netstandard2.0 (DriverBase.cs:184 says so explicitly). Move 13 must convert it to unchecked 32-bit TickCount arithmetic, at which point the `_cachedAtMs == 0 ? null` never-snapshotted sentinel (BeckhoffDriver.cs:57) becomes ambiguous — TickCount is legitimately 0 at wrap. This move inherits whatever that rewrite gets wrong, and its own gate cannot see it.

moves.title: A TwinCAT probe against a dead XAE marks degraded instead of re-stamping the freshness clock
moves.what: `BeckhoffDriver.SnapshotHealth` stops reading and DISCARDING `ProbeIdeAlive()`: when the DTE does not answer it throws, so `RunOnStaThread` never reaches `Volatile.Write(ref _lastOkTick, …)` and `RunProbeOnce`'s `OnProbeFailed` logs and calls `MarkDegraded`. Scope the throw to the `ProbeIdeAlive` verdict specifically, never to any exception inside `SnapshotHealth`. OLD behaviour: `_lastOkTick` is documented as 'the last IDE call that RESPONDED' but `MarshalToIdeThread` on TwinCAT is `StaDispatcher.Run` — a round-trip of the WORKER's own in-process queue that never consults the XAE — and `SnapshotHealth` cannot throw on a dead IDE because `ideAlive` is read and discarded unless it is CLEARING degraded. So the clock re-stamps every ~5s against a dead XAE and `DeriveServedStatus`'s `lastOkAgeMs > StaleMs` branch is unreachable in production. NEW behaviour: a dead channel demotes to `degraded` within the staleness window. Observed by: an engineer whose TcXaeShell hangs or re-registers its DTE while nothing is syncing, whose tray today stays green for minutes and whose only signal is the next `volt push` failing.
moves.why: The signal built specifically to catch 'a silent channel drop (no op, no response)' cannot see the one failure mode it names, and `health` is the ONE ambient poll — so the only writer of the freshness clock is the probe that cannot fail.
closes: _lastOkTick measures the dispatcher round-trip, not an IDE response — so DeriveServedStatus's staleness demotion can never fire
moves.standsAlone: Depends on moves 12 and 13. The product change is contained to one method in one driver; CODESYS is untouched (in-proc, never degrades by design). The degraded flag is not sticky — the next successful snapshot clears it — so a transient miss self-heals as it does today.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Engine.Tests`: `A_probe_whose_IDE_does_not_answer_demotes_the_served_row_to_degraded_and_does_not_restamp_freshness` over a DriverBase-derived driver whose `SnapshotHealth` throws. Red today (the row stays healthy forever).
moves.riskiestPart: `ProbeIdeAlive` is `try { var _ = (int)_dte.Solution.Count; return true; } catch { return false; }` — a cross-process COM read that also returns false for a merely BUSY XAE, not a dead one. Making it fatal risks flapping `degraded` on every long push. Mitigation: `degraded` is not sticky and `_opInFlight > 0` already short-circuits `DeriveServedStatus` to healthy while a client op holds the thread — but the interaction between an in-flight op and a CONCURRENT probe must be re-read before landing. This move does NOT close the `_opInFlight` note at DriverBase.cs:33-38 (a wedged probe pins the counter and defeats the fix); carry that note forward rather than deleting it.

moves.what: `BridgePipeHost`'s `Ops.Connect` arm adds, after the `IsConnected` check, a comparison of `_ide.ServedProjectName` to a NON-EMPTY `sel.Project` (Ordinal, matching `OpGuard`), refusing with the same `PLC_DISCONNECTED` and the existing inline message. Observed by: a connector session declaring interest in project B on a two-project TwinCAT XAE where the driver attaches A — today `ConnectionManager` marks B connected, the UI shows a green row for B, and the user's first push refuses WRONG_PROJECT against a bridge the UI just called connected.
