moves.title: CODESYS's unhandled-kind manifest carries the item name, like TwinCAT's, and logs the missing reader
moves.what: `CodesysDriver.Code.ReadManifest`'s trailing `: $"{kind}\n"` becomes `: NameManifest(item, kind)` — `$"Name={_om.GetName(item.Native)}\n"`, the SAME shape `BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs:44-62` already produces for an arbitrary kind — plus a once-per-kind `VoltLog.Warn` naming the kind that has no descriptor reader. The kind-stamped constant is kept for the genuinely metadata-free case and hoisted to `ItemKind.EmptyManifest(kind)`, which both drivers call — this retires the `ponytail:` note at `ICodeStore.cs:39-43`, whose stated upgrade path is exactly that helper. `ICodeStore`'s doc is updated: the constant is for an item with NO metadata, and a classified kind with no reader is LOGGED. OLD behaviour: CODESYS classifies `IVisualObject`, `IImagePoolObject` and `IGlobalTextListObject` as tracked items, none has a descriptor reader, and all fall through to a constant — so 40 visualizations in one folder all hash IDENTICALLY, `volt status` says clean forever, and the same project versions DIFFERENTLY on the two vendors. NEW behaviour: name-derived content on both vendors, per-item version distinctness, and the missing reader in the log instead of hidden behind a fallback. Observed by: a CODESYS user, ONCE — those files' bytes change on the next pull.
moves.why: `ICodeStore.cs:33-37` calls this value PARITY-CRITICAL because `Hasher` takes the item's content version from it. This is the only one of the three candidate answers that does not injure a user: seam-first's throw hard-fails `volt pull` on most real CODESYS projects, and delete-first's untracking deletes files from repositories the user owns AND edits the extension tables `bun run check` cross-asserts across four runtimes — a gate outside this change's per-move contract.
closes: The final bytes of every NON-SOURCE workspace file are decided below the driver seam with a silent fallback, so most reference kinds materialize as a constant that can never change version
moves.standsAlone: One expression per driver plus a Core helper. `_om.GetName` is already used by `CodesysDriver.WriteXml`, so no new object-model surface is touched. This move does NOT edit `ItemKind`'s extension tables, so `bun run check` is unaffected.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Engine.Tests`: `Two_differently_named_items_of_one_unhandled_kind_hash_to_different_versions` — red today (both hash the same constant). PLUS a live CODESYS e2e, which will report one-time content changes on the affected files.
moves.riskiestPart: This is a one-time byte change to every `.visualization`/`.image_pool`/`.text_list`/`.class_diagram` file in every existing CODESYS workspace: the first `volt pull` after the update reports them all as changed. That is a real, visible churn commit for users. Be honest that it is a PARTIAL fix — it restores per-item distinctness and vendor parity, but a user editing MainVisu still sees no change until a vendor descriptor reader exists, which needs a live CODESYS and is out of this phase's reach.
moves.source: minimal-move (explicitly preferred over both alternatives by judges 1 and 3)
objections: [invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: If the majority lets it through, split it and ship only the half that is provable. Safe form (a) — a pure shape move: hoist the constant to `ItemKind.EmptyManifest(kind)` called by BOTH drivers and add the missing-reader log, changing NO bytes. That retires the ponytail note at ICodeStore.cs:39-43 honestly, has zero user churn, zero parity risk, and no fake red-first test is needed. Safe form (b) — if the name must go into the body, then the SAME PREDICATE must govern both vendors in the same commit: TwinCAT must also emit `Name=<name>\n` on the empty-ProduceXml path (it can — BeckhoffDriver already holds the node) so the constant becomes genuinely unreachable on both sides, and the move text must state the fix is PARTIAL (content is still unversioned) as target.md §17 does and the handed-down row does not. The one thing to watch either way: TcObjectModel.cs:354's `?? \"\"` branch. Nothing offline can tell you how often it fires, and it is the exact line that decides whether this move creates or removes a vendor-detectable manifest.

[invariants] objection: Check 2 — load-bearing asymmetry / vendor parity: the move INTRODUCES a new CODESYS↔TwinCAT manifest divergence in exactly the item class it targets. After the change the two vendors select the kind-stamped constant by DIFFERENT predicates: CODESYS by 'this kind has no descriptor reader' (static, kind-keyed — CodesysDriver.Code.cs:44-52), TwinCAT by 'ProduceXml() returned empty' (runtime, item-keyed — BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs:48-49 over TcObjectModel.cs:354, whose own doc says 'or "" if it produces none'). For any item where TC produces no metadata XML, TwinCAT keeps emitting `text_list\n` while CODESYS now emits `Name=X\n` — where TODAY both emit the byte-identical constant. ICodeStore.cs:34-37 calls this exact value PARITY-CRITICAL and requires byte-identical manifests on both vendors, because Materializer.cs:24 writes it verbatim into the user's repo and Hasher.ComputeItemVersion takes the version from it. Consequence, and the direct answer to my specialist question: a pipe client can still tell which vendor it is talking to from a `fetch` sourceText — and now in a place where it previously could not.

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — red-first test: the named gate test `Two_differently_named_items_of_one_unhandled_kind_hash_to_different_versions` in test/Volt.Engine.Tests/HasherTests.cs CANNOT be red today, because it cannot reach the changed code. Volt.Engine.Tests.csproj is net8.0 and ProjectReferences ONLY Volt.Engine; Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys.csproj is net48 OutputType=Library; and a grep of the whole test/ tree for `Volt.Cli.Ide` returns ZERO hits — no suite references either driver. Anything writable in HasherTests is a tautology over Hasher.ComputeItemVersion("f","Name=A\n") vs ("f","Name=B\n"), which is GREEN today and already asserted at HasherTests.cs:24-25. The only way to make it red is to edit test/shared/FakeIde.cs:217 (`ReadManifest => Find(item).Declaration ?? ""`) so the shared fake imitates a driver fallback it does not model — a fake compiled into three suites, and the textbook 'fakes assert the bug away' failure. Consequence: the move's stated gate proves nothing; the whole change rides on one live CODESYS run.

[invariants] objection: Check 8 — stands alone / undeclared blast radius: the move row says ONE file and 'One method's fallback branch'. Its own source, target.md §17, names FIVE — CodesysDriver.Code.cs, BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs, ItemKind.cs, ICodeStore.cs, HasherTests.cs — plus a `VoltLog.Warn` with once-per-kind dedup, i.e. NEW MUTABLE STATE in a type map.md records as having 'none of its own; every member is a stateless projection'. That state lives in a net48 DLL the CODESYS IDE loads once in-process, so a static dedup set is shared across every session and mutated on the fetch path. A move whose entire warrant is 'stands alone' understating its own file list by 4 files and one piece of state is disqualifying on its face.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — ARCHITECTURE §Conventions, twice. (a) Second answer to one question: hoisting the STRING to ItemKind.EmptyManifest while leaving the PREDICATE that selects it per-vendor and different is precisely the drift the helper claims to retire; the ponytail note at ICodeStore.cs:39-43 asks that the CODESYS fall-through be decided LOUDLY, and this decides it quietly. (b) Defensive default / `?? guess`: `Name=<name>\n` fabricates content out of identity. The name is already the FILE NAME (Materializer.FullWireName), so the manifest gains zero information — and it makes a missing descriptor reader byte-indistinguishable from a vendor that genuinely exposes one metadata field. Today `visualization\n` visibly announces 'nothing is recorded here'; after the move the file looks like a real manifest. The only counter-signal is a Warn in %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Volt\\logs (VoltLog.cs:88, file-append only) — I found no component that reads it: volt-control has no log reader, and the Diagnostics view does not surface it.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 — the named behavior change does not achieve its stated 'why'. The row's why is 'their content version can never change — Hasher takes the item version from this text.' That statement is still TRUE after the fix: the manifest still carries no visualization content, so a user editing MainVisu still sees no version change. target.md §17 concedes this ('Be honest that it is a PARTIAL fix'); the row handed to me does not. Meanwhile the identical-hash symptom it does fix is inert — FetchService.cs:79-120 keys versions by item NAME, and I found no code that keys, dedups or compares on the version VALUE across items, so identical versions for distinct names cause no defect. Net: the only certain effect is a one-time rewrite of every .visualization/.image_pool/.text_list file in every existing CODESYS workspace, in exchange for nothing a user can observe.

[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Split it. The log line is the only half that carries information, and it costs nobody a byte: ship `VoltLog.Warn` alone (once per kind, guarded by process-static state), keep `$"{kind}\n"`, and the finding's real complaint — "nothing anywhere logs that fact" — is closed with zero blast radius, no churn commit, and no unwritable red-first test. Hold the `Name=` byte change until the three descriptor readers exist: those readers will change the same bytes again, so landing this now bills every CODESYS user TWO churn commits in repositories Volt does not own, to reach a state where MainVisu still versions as a constant. If the majority lets the byte change through anyway, the one thing to watch is that `_om.GetName(item.Native)` is a NEW reflection call on a path that previously could not fail — Versioning.Materialize is deliberately no-catch for single-item paths, so a GetName fault now turns a guaranteed-succeed manifest into a thrown op; and require the move to carry ItemKind.cs, ICodeStore.cs and BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs in the same commit, or ICodeStore's pinned contract ships contradicting both drivers.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — the row lists ONE file, but the design it implements (target.md:479-483) explicitly requires `ItemKind.EmptyManifest` hoisted into Volt.Engine/Workspace/ItemKind.cs, BOTH drivers calling it (BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs:49 currently hand-writes `$"{kind}\n"`), and ICodeStore.cs:33-43's doc + ponytail note rewritten. That is 4 files, not 1. Applied exactly as the row is written, the solution does not build.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (red-first test) — the named red-first test on the manifest bytes cannot be written. No .csproj in the repo references Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys (verified against Volt.Cli.sln and all four test csprojs), and all four test projects are net8.0 while Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys is net48, so a ProjectReference is not even restorable. FakeIde.cs:217 (`Declaration ?? ""`) and GraphicalCodeTests.cs:245 (`throw new NotSupportedException()`) are the only ReadManifest implementations any suite can reach — neither is the code being changed. This is verbatim the ground on which target.md:758 disqualified the sibling move `probe-partial-enumeration-fails` ("no test project in the repo references Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat"); the same disqualifier was not applied here.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (observable change is real but the NAMED benefit is inert) — the move's `why` says the content version 'can never change'. `Name=MainVisu\n` is just as constant as `visualization\n`: after the fix, an engineer editing MainVisu STILL sees no change, forever. target.md:496 concedes this ('PARTIAL'). The one thing actually delivered — per-item hash distinctness — is provably unused: Hasher.ComputeItemVersion(folder, text) feeds only (a) FetchService.cs:127 `knownItems.TryGetValue(fullName, ...) && known == version`, a per-NAME comparison, and (b) Hasher.ComputeProjectVersion, which already appends `name:version` per line, so the name is ALREADY in the project-version basis. No consumer anywhere compares versions across different item names. Two visualizations hashing identically has zero consequence. So the move imposes a real cost (a churn commit rewriting every .visualization/.text_list/.image_pool/.class_diagram/.parameter_list/.external_types/.tmc file in every existing CODESYS workspace) for zero observable benefit, and redundantly: the item name is already the workspace FILE name (Materializer.cs:22-29 `FullWireName(name, ext)`).

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (ARCHITECTURE.md §Conventions rule 3, 'one question, one answer') — 'what is the manifest for an item with no descriptor' gains a second answer decided by vendor-specific criteria: CODESYS by an implicit allowlist (whichever kinds happen to have a ternary arm), TwinCAT by `string.IsNullOrEmpty(ProduceXml(...))` (BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs:49). The hoisted `ItemKind.EmptyManifest` would then have exactly ONE caller (TwinCAT), since CODESYS's fallback no longer reaches it. And if the move really touches only CodesysDriver.Code.cs, ICodeStore.cs:37-39 still pins `"{kind}\n"` as THE canonical body and calls the manifest PARITY-CRITICAL — the interface contract would openly contradict its implementation.

[hidden] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Carry this objection: the changed line is executed by NOTHING except CODESYS's IronPython load path, so 'build + 3 suites' is not evidence — it is silence. The narrower safe form: (1) keep the single expression change AND edit ICodeStore.cs:36-43 in the same commit so the contract text and the ponytail note stop describing behaviour that no longer exists; (2) move the red-first proof to the only layer that can run it — an assertion in `bun test test/e2e` on the fetch response's sourceText for a `.visualization` item against the headless CODESYS fixture (pwsh scripts/codesys-pipe.ps1 up, VOLT_PIPE=volt.bridge.codesys) — and explicitly forbid the alternative of teaching test/shared/FakeIde.cs:217 the `$\"{kind}\\n\"` constant to manufacture a red Hasher test; (3) route the gap line through VoltLog, never Console.Error (the CodesysTypeMap:124 / CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44 precedent is the wrong one to copy), and key the once-only gate per connect rather than per process, since the DLL outlives PipeHost.Stop()/Start() inside a running IDE. The one thing to watch at runtime: `CodesysObjectModel.GetName` ends in `?? \"\"`, so verify on the live IDE that no affected item materializes as `Name=\\n` — if any does, the fix has moved the bug rather than fixed it, and nothing in the per-kind warning will tell you.

[hidden] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first test cannot be written where the gate puts it. The gate is 'red-first test on the manifest bytes' in Volt.Engine.Tests (target.md:494, `Two_differently_named_items_of_one_unhandled_kind_hash_to_different_versions`). The changed expression lives in Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys, and NO test project references that assembly: test/Volt.Engine.Tests.csproj references only src/Volt.Engine; test/Volt.Cli.Tests.csproj references Volt.Engine + Volt.Cli.Transport + Volt.Cli; map.md's PipeHost row states outright '(no STATIC C# callers anywhere in src/ or test/ — no .csproj in the repo references this project; it appears only in Volt.Cli.sln:16)' and the CodesysTypeMap row repeats it ('No STATIC test callers … the only exercise is the live e2e run'). The only ICodeStore a Volt.Engine.Tests test can reach is test/shared/FakeIde.cs:217 `public string ReadManifest(ItemRef item, string kind) => Find(item).Declaration ?? "";` — which has no kind fallback at all, so two differently-named items with different Declarations ALREADY hash differently and the named test is GREEN today, not red. Consequence: to make it red you must edit FakeIde to emulate the CODESYS constant, i.e. teach the one shared fake (compiled into every suite) the bug the fix removes — the exact failure mode the repo's own policy names ('fakes can assert a bug away'). Either the gate is unexecutable as written or it is satisfied by a fake edit that proves nothing about the live driver.

[hidden] objection: Check 8 — 'stands alone' is stated at the wrong size, and the three suites pass VACUOUSLY. The move row I was given says files = CodesysDriver.Code.cs only and 'One method's fallback branch'; target.md:490 for the same move lists FIVE files across three projects (CodesysDriver.Code.cs, BeckhoffDriver.Code.cs, Volt.Engine/Workspace/ItemKind.cs, Volt.Engine/Ide/ICodeStore.cs, test/Volt.Engine.Tests/HasherTests.cs) because it also hoists the kept constant to `ItemKind.EmptyManifest(kind)` that BOTH drivers call. Consequence if the one-file version is implemented: ICodeStore.cs:36-38 still states the contract 'An item whose vendor exposes no metadata for this kind yields the canonical kind-stamped body "{kind}\n"' and the ponytail note at :39-43 still claims the fallback is the CODESYS behaviour — the shipped code then contradicts its own written contract in the file every future driver author reads. Consequence if the five-file version is implemented: it is a cross-project edit touching both vendors' wire-observable manifest, not 'one method's fallback branch', and the byte-identity of the Beckhoff swap (`$"{kind}\n"` → `ItemKind.EmptyManifest(kind)`) is asserted by no test either, since Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat is equally unreferenced by every test csproj. In both cases `dotnet test` × 3 goes green whether the change works, no-ops, or throws.

[hidden] objection: Check 4 — the 'and logs the gap' half is a background failure that stays effectively swallowed. The only precedent for a once-per-X warning in this assembly is CodesysTypeMap.WarnUnrecognized, and map.md:238 records both of its traits: it 'writes to Console.Error (:124), not VoltLog — a second, unmonitored log channel (same divergence at CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:44)', and its `_loggedUnknown` gate is 'a process-lifetime HashSet … never cleared, so a PipeHost.Stop()/Start() cycle does not reset the once-per-signature warning (the assembly stays loaded in the IDE)'. Consequence: copy that precedent and the missing-reader line goes to CODESYS's console instead of %LOCALAPPDATA%\Volt\logs — the one place docs/debugging-a-bridge-session.md tells a user to look; keep it once-per-process and a support session that restarts the bridge inside a long-running IDE gets nothing, because the DLL and its static gate outlive the restart. The move's stated benefit ('the missing reader in the log instead of hidden behind a fallback') is then not delivered, while the byte churn is.

moves.title: One parser decides a POU's kind from its declaration text
moves.what: Add `ItemKind.CodeForDeclaration(decl)` in Core, implemented over the existing `CodeHelper.ParseCodeHeader` (which already walks past `{` pragmas, `//` and `(* *)` blocks before reading the keyword), and point `CodesysTypeMap.RefinePou` at it. Delete `LeadingKeyword` and `CodesysTypeMap.NeedsDeclaration`'s hand-maintained mirror of the `RefinePou` branch. An unmapped `CodeHelper` result falls back to today's `PlcPouFb` default — it must NEVER throw mid-walk. OLD behaviour: `LeadingKeyword` reads the first token from a raw `TrimStart`, so a declaration opening with `{attribute 'qualified_only'}` or a doc header yields `""` and `RefinePou` falls to `return ItemKind.PlcPouFb`. For a real INTERFACE that flips the driver's classification, and `CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24` re-asks the same classifier to choose the export primitive — so a commented interface is exported down the NON-interface path while `Materializer`, using the Core parser on the same text, still names the file `.itf`. Nothing throws. NEW behaviour: one parser, one verdict. Observed by: any CODESYS user who puts an attribute pragma or a doc header above an INTERFACE.
moves.why: The wrong verdict selects which vendor export primitive runs, so the item materializes from the wrong export, silently, into the user's workspace. Moving the decision into Core is also the ONLY way it becomes testable at all — no test .csproj references `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys`, so the duplicate lives where a test cannot reach it.
closes: Two parsers derive a POU's kind from the same declaration text, and only one of them knows that a declaration may start with a pragma or a comment
moves.standsAlone: The new Core helper is testable offline, which is the whole point. `CodesysTypeMap`'s call-site swap is compiler-checked; the deleted `LeadingKeyword` has no other consumer.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Engine.Tests`: `A_declaration_opening_with_a_pragma_or_a_doc_comment_classifies_as_INTERFACE` — red today. PLUS a live CODESYS e2e, because the driver-side call site cannot be pinned offline.
moves.riskiestPart: `CodeHelper` returns kind STRINGS while `CodesysTypeMap` returns numeric `ItemKind` codes. The mapping between them must be exhaustive, and an unmapped result MUST fall back to today's `PlcPouFb` default rather than throwing mid-walk — a throw here would abort a tree walk on a live project.
moves.source: seam-first (grafted by all three judges; neither other candidate touches it)
objections: [invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Carry this objection: the parser being substituted THROWS and the one being replaced does not, and the substitution point is upstream of the only guard that contains that throw. If the majority lets it through, the narrower safe form is: (1) do NOT call `ParseCodeHeader` from `RefinePou`. Instead extract only its header-line SELECTION (the pragma/comment skip loop, CodeHelper.cs:24-42) into a public total helper in Volt.Engine — `CodeHelper.HeaderLine(string?) -> string` returning `""` when no header exists — and have `LeadingKeyword` consume that. `RefinePou` keeps its existing four-arm keyword switch and its `PlcPouFb` default, so the classifier stays total, its output domain stays 602/603/604/618, no inverse kind→code table is needed, and no new BridgeErrorCode can escape the CODESYS walk. That closes the actual defect (the pragma/comment blindness) and leaves nothing else moving. (2) The single thing to watch either way: `CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24` — the classifier is also the export-primitive selector, so any verdict flip changes emitted XML and therefore git SHAs on an existing workspace. Whatever the shape, the gate must include an item whose declaration begins with `{attribute 'qualified_only'}` AND one whose declaration is empty (`ReadAspectText` returned `""`), and it must prove `refs` still returns a full tree for the second. Since no headless suite can reach `CodesysTypeMap` today, that gate is a live-CODESYS e2e run (`codesys-pipe.ps1` + `bun test test/e2e`), and the move should say so instead of claiming "build + 3 suites".

[invariants] objection: Check 1 — observable deltas beyond the one named. The move names only "the kind an existing workspace records changes". There are at least two more. (a) CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24 re-asks the same classifier to pick the EXPORT PRIMITIVE — `if (KindCodeOf(item.Native) == ItemKind.PlcItf) return _om.ExportInterfaceXml(...); return _om.ExportXmlWithChildren(...)` — so any item whose verdict flips also changes which PLCopen XML the bridge produces, hence the assembled ST body text, hence the git object SHA of the file in `src/`. That is a content change on a live-PLC round-trip path, not a metadata change. (b) The `refs`/`fetch` wire `kind` string flips `function_block` → `interface` for those items, which volt-control / the LSP / the VS Code manifest consume. Consequence: an unnamed content delta on the push path — the item recorded as `.fb` in an existing repo starts round-tripping through a different vendor export primitive.

[invariants] objection: Check 2 — it makes a load-bearing asymmetry fatal, and the answer to the specialist question becomes YES. `CodeHelper.ParseCodeHeader` is a PARTIAL function: it throws `BridgeException(BridgeErrorCodes.InvalidCodeHeader)` on empty/whitespace input (CodeHelper.cs:18-19) and on any unrecognized header (CodeHelper.cs:73-74, pinned by CodeHelperTests.cs:85). `RefinePou` is TOTAL — every input returns a code (CodesysTypeMap.cs:161 `return ItemKind.PlcPouFb; // default`). Its input is `CodesysObjectModel.ReadAspectText(iobj, "Interface")`, which returns `""` whenever the aspect or its TextDocument is absent (CodesysObjectModel.cs:249-256) — reachable for an IPOUObject whose declaration is not readable. That call sits in `CodesysDriver.KindCodeOf` (Tree.cs:150-151), invoked per child from `Walk` (Tree.cs:48). `Walk`'s ONLY try/catch is around `_om.GetChildren` (Tree.cs:43-44); the per-child classify is unguarded, and `ProjectSnapshot.Walk` calls `ide.WalkItems()` to completion (ProjectSnapshot.cs:60) BEFORE the per-item guard `Versioning.SafeVersion` (Versioning.cs:33-34) — the guard that exists precisely because `Materializer` calls the same `ParseCodeHeader`. So one unreadable POU declaration turns the whole `refs`/`fetch`/push-receipt into an `INVALID_CODE_HEADER` failure. BeckhoffDriver classifies with `_om.ItemType(node)` (BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:134), which cannot raise a parse error, and its unmapped codes fall to `snap.Unmapped++` and are skipped. Consequence, and the specialist answer: after this move a pipe client CAN tell the vendor — the same corpus item yields a whole-project op failure with a named BridgeErrorCode on CODESYS and a silent per-item skip on TwinCAT. Moving the parser upstream of the one guard designed to contain its throw is the regression.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — §Conventions, whichever way the throw is resolved. Containing the new failure mode means either wrapping the call in try/catch and falling back to `PlcPouFb` (a defensive `?? guess`, exactly what the no-fallbacks rule forbids) or letting it throw (check 2). Separately, `ParseCodeHeader` returns `ItemKind.Kinds` STRINGS while `RefinePou` returns int codes, and `ItemKind.Map` is code→string only — there is no inverse. The move therefore has to introduce a string→code table. Put it in `CodesysTypeMap` and it re-spells centralized `ItemKind.Kinds` vocabulary outside its home file; put it in `ItemKind` and it is a second answer to the question `Map` already answers, and the move is no longer "one call site". Also unhandled: `ParseCodeHeader`'s output domain is far wider than `RefinePou`'s four codes (Gvl, Dut, Action, Method, Property are all reachable returns), and every downstream consumer — `ItemKind.ExtFor`, `IsTopLevelCrud`, the `PlcItf` export branch — was only ever fed 602/603/604/618. The move names no arm for the widened domain.

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first test cannot be written in any of the three gate suites. `CodesysTypeMap` is `internal static` (CodesysTypeMap.cs:15) inside `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys`, which is `<TargetFramework>net48</TargetFramework>`. All three C# suites are `net8.0` and NONE of them references that project: Volt.Cli.Tests → Volt.Engine, Volt.Cli.Transport, Volt.Cli; Volt.Engine.Tests → Volt.Engine; Volt.Cli.Connector.Tests → Volt.Cli.Connector.Core, Volt.Engine. There is no `InternalsVisibleTo`. The only harness that can exercise `RefinePou` is `bun test test/e2e` against a LIVE CODESYS IDE via `codesys-pipe.ps1` — not a headless suite. So "red-first test on a declaration the two parsers classify differently" requires either a new test-only seam (public/InternalsVisibleTo + a net48-compatible test project) or a live IDE, neither of which the move declares.

[invariants] objection: Check 8 / gate adequacy — the stated gate is vacuous. "build + 3 suites" cannot fail for this change, because no suite compiles against the file being changed. The gate would go green while carrying the check-2 regression. A move whose gate is structurally incapable of detecting its own named risk does not stand alone.

[invariants] objection: Scoping — the declared blast radius is wrong. `files: packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Engine/`, but the defect and the call site are `packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys/Ide/CodesysTypeMap.cs:154,167` and its consumer `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys/Driver/CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24`. A reviewer approving a Volt.Engine-only diff would get a change to the net48 in-proc CODESYS host. If instead the intent is to MOVE the refinement into Volt.Engine, that is a type move across the vendor seam that changes `CodesysTypeMap`'s surface and drags `NeedsDeclaration` (Tree.cs:149 relies on the two staying co-located as a "single-file invariant") — not "substitutes the shared parser at one call site".

[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Do not delete `NeedsDeclaration`, and do not add `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs`'s aspect read to every node. The narrow safe form is: add `CodeHelper.TryParseCodeHeader(string? code, out CodeHeader header)` in Core — non-throwing, so the fallback policy is owned once and explicitly, with a VoltLog line naming the item — plus `ItemKind.CodeForDeclaration` built by INVERTING `ItemKind.Map` rather than hand-writing a second string→code table; then `RefinePou` becomes one call. `CodesysTypeMap` stays the only edited file below Core, `NeedsDeclaration` stays, and `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs`/`Code.cs` are untouched, so the commit actually compiles alone. The one thing to watch: before believing this fixes anything, get a live CODESYS `/debug` TypeTags dump of a real INTERFACE object — if `IInterfaceObject` arrives without `IPOUObject`, line 46 never fires for interfaces, RefinePou's INTERFACE branch is dead, and this is a shape move mislabeled as a fix. And whatever ships must be re-checked against the wire: the `kind` string on refs/fetch changes for any item whose classification flips, which is a wire-blast-radius change the move currently does not declare.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — FIRST COMPILE ERROR. The move says "Delete LeadingKeyword and CodesysTypeMap.NeedsDeclaration's hand-maintained mirror". `NeedsDeclaration` has exactly ONE caller repo-wide: packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys/Driver/CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:150 — a file ABSENT from the move's Files list. Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys (net48) is in Volt.Cli.sln and compiles after Volt.Engine, so applying the move exactly as written yields, as its first error: CS0117 'CodesysTypeMap' does not contain a definition for 'NeedsDeclaration' at CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:150. Consequence: `dotnet build Volt.Cli.sln -c Release` fails; the commit does not stand alone. And the deletion is not achievable even with Tree.cs added: the mirror IS `Has(ifaces,"IPOUObject")` — CODESYS interface-name knowledge that Core (vendor-neutral, guarded by VendorParityGuardTests) cannot own. Drop the gate and Tree.cs does a reflection ReadAspectText round-trip for EVERY node in the walk (an unnamed latency regression on a Hauzer-scale project); keep a local check and the mirror is relocated, not deleted.

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (no swallow / one error channel) + Check 2 (the CODESYS walk has no per-node catch). The move's stated mitigation is physically impossible: CodeHelper.ParseCodeHeader NEVER returns an unmapped result — it THROWS BridgeException(BridgeErrorCodes.InvalidCodeHeader) on three paths (CodeHelper.cs:19 empty/whitespace, :45 no header line, :73 unrecognized header). So "an unmapped CodeHelper result falls back to today's PlcPouFb" covers a case that cannot occur and omits the case that will. CodesysObjectModel.ReadAspectText returns "" — never null — whenever the Interface aspect / TextDocument / Text member read comes back null (CodesysObjectModel.cs:249-256), so "" is a live input and ParseCodeHeader("") throws "Empty code". KindCodeOf is called at CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:47 INSIDE the foreach; the walk's only try/catch guards _om.GetChildren (Tree.cs:43). That is precisely the load-bearing asymmetry check 2 names — Beckhoff has a per-node catch, CODESYS deliberately does not. Consequence: one POU whose declaration CodeHelper cannot parse aborts the entire refs/fetch with INVALID_CODE_HEADER, from a move whose own riskiest-part says it must never throw mid-walk. CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24 re-invokes KindCodeOf inside ReadXml, so the same throw also kills a per-item push/pull. Honoring the contract forces `catch (BridgeException) { return PlcPouFb; }` inside Core — a new silent swallow at a parity-critical decision (conventions 1/4/5) — and leaves the SAME parser with two opposite error policies, since Materializer.cs:57/67 lets that exception propagate. "One parser, one verdict" is not delivered.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (red-first test). `A_declaration_opening_with_a_pragma_or_a_doc_comment_classifies_as_INTERFACE` in Volt.Engine.Tests targets ItemKind.CodeForDeclaration, which does not exist today — the test does not COMPILE before the fix, so it is not red-first, it is born with its own subject. The defect itself lives in CodesysTypeMap.RefinePou: a `private` method on an `internal` class in Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys, and I verified no test csproj references that project (Volt.Engine.Tests → Volt.Engine only; Volt.Cli.Tests → Engine/Transport/Cli only). So the gate proves the new helper parses text and proves NOTHING about the classification change. The move concedes this ("the driver-side call site cannot be pinned offline") and defers to a live CODESYS e2e that is not one of the three suites.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (observable change named). Under-stated and partly unverifiable. The refined code reaches the wire via ItemKind.Map as the `kind` field on refs/fetch, so affected items change WIRE BYTES — the move declares blast radius `cross-project`, not `wire`. It also flips upstream routing (IsSourceKind / IsTopLevelCrud / IsInlinedInPou). Meanwhile Materializer ALREADY derives the file extension independently from CodeHelper (Materializer.cs:67 → ExtFor(resolvedKind)), so the extension is already correct today and only the export primitive is wrong — none of which the move states. Worse, I could NOT verify the headline scenario is reachable at all: CodeForObject checks IPOUObject (CodesysTypeMap.cs:46 → RefinePou) BEFORE IInterfaceObject (:55 → PlcItf), so exactly one of those two branches is dead code, and which one decides whether "a commented INTERFACE is exported down the non-interface path" is a real defect or fiction. That needs a live CODESYS TypeTags read; the move supplies no evidence.

[hidden] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Before writing any code, settle the premise on a live CODESYS: run the `debug` op's `typeTags` (DebugService.cs:106 -> CodesysDriver.TypeTags) against a real INTERFACE object and record whether its set contains `IPOUObject`. If it does NOT, drop the move entirely — the defect is fiction. If it DOES, the safe narrow form is a ONE-LINE reorder in `CodesysTypeMap.CodeForObject`: move the `IInterfaceObject` test (:55) above the `IPOUObject` test (:46). That fixes the only genuinely harmful case (`ReadXml` picking `ExportXmlWithChildren` over `ExportInterfaceXml` for an interface) with no parser, no Core change, no throw risk, no silent fallback, no wire-kind churn on PROGRAM/FUNCTION, and no reflected aspect read added to the walk — and unlike this move it is decided from the vendor's own structural signal rather than from text.

If the parser substitution proceeds anyway, the one thing to watch is the empty declaration: `ReadAspectText` returns `""` by design for a missing aspect (CodesysObjectModel.cs:252-255), and `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:48` calls `KindCodeOf` OUTSIDE the try/catch at :43-44 — so a single such POU throws `INVALID_CODE_HEADER` out of `WalkItems` and takes down `fetch`/`refs`/`init`/`push` for the entire project, on a live PLC. Guarding it with a catch trades that for the opposite failure at `CodesysDriver.Code.cs:24`, where `Versioning.SafeVersion` (Versioning.cs:33-34) converts the throw into `Unreadable` and silently drops the POU's body from the pull behind a Warn line. Whichever is chosen must be a deliberate, commented decision at BOTH call sites, and the `--json` gate must be re-run against a project containing a POU with an empty Interface aspect and one with an unterminated `(*` doc header — the two inputs on which the old and new parsers provably disagree.

[hidden] objection: Check 1 — the observable delta is named WRONG and INCOMPLETE. I verified at Materializer.cs:20-21 that the workspace file EXTENSION is already chosen by `build.Kind`, i.e. by `CodeHelper.ParseCodeHeader` (Materializer.cs:67), not by the driver's `RefinePou`. So for a pragma-/comment-headed PROGRAM or FUNCTION the file is ALREADY `.prg`/`.fun` and the content is already right (`ReadXml` takes the same `ExportXmlWithChildren` branch either way, Code.cs:24-25). What actually changes for that whole class of items is only the **wire `kind` string** reported by `refs`/`fetch` (FetchService.cs:78 `ItemKind.Map(it.KindCode)`) — flipping `function_block` to `program`/`function` for every such POU. That is a pipe-wire byte change on items the move never mentions, consumed by name in TypeScript (volt-control, LSP, volt-vscode — map.md:184 records `Kinds` values as a cross-language contract with no C# reference). An unnamed wire-kind delta on an unnamed item class is exactly the defect check 1 exists to catch.

[hidden] objection: Check 4 — the move's own mandated mitigation is a convention-1 violation, and it defeats the move's headline. `CodeHelper.ParseCodeHeader` does not return an 'unmapped result' — it THROWS `BridgeException(InvalidCodeHeader)` on empty/whitespace input (CodeHelper.cs:18-19), on a header line it cannot find (`:44-45`), and on an unrecognised keyword (`:73-74`; pinned by CodeHelperTests.cs:85). The move requires it to 'NEVER throw mid-walk and fall back to today's PlcPouFb', which forces (a) a `catch` swallowing a coded BridgeException inside Core and (b) a silent default for the kind strings `CodeHelper` legitimately returns that have no POU code (`gvl`, `dut`, `action`, `method`, `property` — map.md:189 records that `ExtFor` already throws on `method`/`property` from this same parser). ARCHITECTURE.md:219-223 convention 1 verbatim: 'No fallbacks. Fail loud with a coded error. A defensive default (`?? ""`, `?? "FBD"`, a silent `catch`) masks a bug somewhere else and buys nothing.' Convention 5 (`:234`) forbids the swallow of the one error channel. And with that catch, `CodeForDeclaration` still owns a second, hand-written classification rule — so 'one parser, one verdict' is false; the second answer is just relocated into Core where it is harder to see.

[hidden] objection: Check 7 — the named red-first test cannot be red. `A_declaration_opening_with_a_pragma_or_a_doc_comment_classifies_as_INTERFACE` is placed in `Volt.Engine.Tests`, where the only thing it can call is the NEW `ItemKind.CodeForDeclaration`. That symbol does not exist today, so the test does not compile today, let alone fail — it is a green-on-arrival test of new code, not a pin on the defect. I confirmed the defect stays untestable after the move: `grep -rn 'Ide.Codesys' --include=*.csproj packages/volt-cli/` returns exactly one hit, the project's own `<RootNamespace>` — no test .csproj references `Volt.Cli.Ide.Codesys` (map.md:238 states the same: 'No STATIC test callers … the only exercise is the live e2e run'). The move's gate concedes this ('the driver-side call site cannot be pinned offline') and leans on a live CODESYS e2e which findings.md documents as the local-only suite that is currently parked.

[hidden] objection: Check 8 — it does not stand alone; two call sites with opposite failure modes, and one deletion that is not what it says. (a) `CodesysDriver.ReadXml` (Code.cs:24) re-runs `KindCodeOf` per POU on the BODY path, and there `Versioning.SafeVersion` catches everything (Versioning.cs:33-34) and returns `Unreadable` — so a throw there does not fail loudly, it silently DROPS the POU's body from the pull with only a Warn line. On the WALK path (`CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:48`) the same throw is unguarded — the `try/catch` at Tree.cs:43-44 wraps only `_om.GetChildren`, so it aborts `WalkItems` and every `fetch`/`refs`/`init`/`push` for the whole project. One change, two opposite blast radii, only one acknowledged. (b) The move says to delete `CodesysTypeMap.NeedsDeclaration`'s 'hand-maintained mirror'. `NeedsDeclaration` is not a mirror body — it is `Has(ifaces, "IPOUObject")` (CodesysTypeMap.cs:131-132) and it is the GATE at `CodesysDriver.Tree.cs:150` that decides whether the reflected `ReadAspectText(iobj, "Interface")` is paid at all. Deleting it forces a reflection aspect read on every node of the walk (devices, tasks, visualizations, library refs — ~880 items on the cited Hauzer project) inside the IDE's own message loop. The wording is ambiguous about the single deletion that is dangerous.

[hidden] objection: PREMISE UNVERIFIED (counts against per the posture) — the headline defect may not exist. `CodesysTypeMap.CodeForObject` reaches `RefinePou` only via `IPOUObject` at :46, while a real interface is classified at :55 via `IInterfaceObject`. `CodesysObjectModel.cs:797-798` and `:808` state flatly that 'CODESYS `export_xml` only works for `IPOUObject`, not `IInterfaceObject`' — which reads as the two being DISJOINT. If they are, a real INTERFACE never reaches `RefinePou` at all, its `INTERFACE` branch is dead, `ReadXml`'s `== ItemKind.PlcItf` test (Code.cs:24) already works from the interface-name set with no declaration involved, and the entire 'wrong export primitive' story the move is built on is fiction. The interface-name set is produced at runtime by reflection (`ObjectInterfaceNames`, map.md:238: 'nothing in the compiler connects the two') and I found NO recorded fixture anywhere in the repo pinning what a CODESYS interface object's interface set contains — I grepped `IPOUObject|IInterfaceObject` repo-wide across every file type and every hit is source or prose, none a fixture. This is unresolvable without a live CODESYS `TypeTags` read, and it is the move's load-bearing premise.

moves.title: Both CLI refusal carriers implement ICodedError, so precondition refusals stay structured
moves.what: `Volt.Cli.Transport.PipeCallException` and `Volt.Cli.Sync.BridgeError` both implement the EXISTING public `ICodedError` (`string ErrorCode => Code;`). `Commands.IsPreconditionRefusal` takes the interface, and the three `catch (PipeCallException e) when (…)` sites at `Commands.cs:175/360/404` become `catch (Exception e) when (e is ICodedError c && IsPreconditionRefusal(c.Code))`. OLD behaviour: PLC_DISCONNECTED reaches the CLI as two exception types with opposite consequences — `PipeCallException` becomes a structured `--json` refusal; `BridgeError` (raised by `BridgeResolver` and `GuardEmptyItems`) matches no catch in `Commands` and falls to `Program.cs:74`, killing the `--json` contract with a stderr line, exit 1 and empty stdout. volt-control renders one as `{kind:"refused"}` and the other as `{kind:"error"}` for situations a user cannot tell apart. NEW behaviour: one code space, one catch. Observed by: an engineer running `volt pull --json` against a genuinely empty PLC project, and any agent branching on the `--json` contract.
moves.why: This is why `ICodedError` is DELIBERATELY not deleted (seam-first's `bridge-exception-down` would have removed it): keeping it makes this a five-line change instead of a new abstraction, and it closes a certain finding both other candidates leave standing.
closes: PLC_DISCONNECTED reaches the CLI as two different exception types with opposite consequences: one becomes a structured refusal, the other kills the --json contract entirely
moves.standsAlone: Adding an interface implementation to two exception types and widening three catch filters. Every case that was a structured refusal stays one; the only change is that three cases that used to escape now do not.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test in `Volt.Cli.Tests`: `Pull_json_against_a_legitimately_empty_project_prints_a_refusal_not_an_error` — assert `{kind:"refused"}` with exit 0, not a bare stderr line with exit 1. Red today.
moves.riskiestPart: `catch (Exception e) when (…)` is broader than `catch (PipeCallException e)`. `BridgeException` (bridge-side) also implements `ICodedError` and never crosses into the CLI process — but `CommandHarness`'s in-process tests run the services DIRECTLY and CAN see it, so the filter must be checked against those tests specifically before landing.
moves.source: minimal-move (judge 3 explicitly instructs keeping ICodedError so this stays cheap)
objections: [invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Split it, and fix the spec before the code. (1) Narrow to the ONLY thing the described edit actually changes: `BridgeClient.GuardEmptyItems`' BridgeError (BridgeClient.cs:67) becoming a structured `{kind:"refused"}` for pull/push/build. Name that as the behavior change, and write the red-first test against `PLC_DISCONNECTED` from an empty fetch — NOT against a resolver refusal, which the edit cannot reach because Program.cs:62 evaluates `Bridge()` outside Commands' try. (2) Assert exit **2**, not 0 — Program.cs:114 returns 2 for any non-Ok `--json` pull, and volt-control ignores the code anyway (actions.ts:103 parses stdout). Any change to that mapping is a separate, separately-named move. (3) Do NOT put `ICodedError` on `PipeCallException`: it is unnecessary for this fix (BridgeError alone is the second carrier) and it is what declares `MALFORMED_ERROR`/`NO_RESULT` as wire codes and widens `PipeServer.cs:90`'s runtime type test. If a shared shape is wanted, give `Commands` an overload taking a bare `string code` and match `e is BridgeError or PipeCallException` explicitly — no interface, no PipeServer blast radius. (4) Either add `AMBIGUOUS_BRIDGE` to `IsPreconditionRefusal` or state in the commit that ambiguity refusals deliberately remain `{kind:"error"}` — do not let the finding read as closed while the two-XAE case is untouched. (5) Whatever ships, update BridgeResolver.cs:19-21 and PipeClient.cs:16-18, whose comments assert the exact opposite of the new arrangement — convention 8 says a false comment is a defect. The one thing to watch after landing: `Program.cs`'s catch ordering, and whether anything now returns a refusal where a hard error was expected on a live PLC.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 (observable change must be NAMED and correct): the move's stated 'why' is factually false, and the named observable is the wrong one. Program.cs:74 is `catch (BridgeError e) { Console.Error.WriteLine(e.Message); return 1; }` — a DEDICATED clause, byte-identical in effect to the PipeCallException clause at Program.cs:75. There is no 'escape to a generic catch'. The author's stated riskiest part ('the CLI's exit code or stderr text changes') names the two things that do NOT change for a resolver refusal (already exit 1 + the message on stderr); the thing that changes is STDOUT — empty today, which is what actions.ts:103 (`parseJson(r.stdout) ?? {kind:"error"}`) turns into `{kind:"error"}`. Consequence: the commit will be gated on an assertion about the wrong stream, and the real delta ships unnamed.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 + Check 8 (the file list cannot produce the change): the move names `Sync/BridgeResolver.cs` and `Program.cs`. `BridgeError` is declared at `Sync/BridgeClient.cs:7`, NOT BridgeResolver.cs; `PipeCallException` at `Transport/PipeMessages.cs:43`; `IsPreconditionRefusal` and the three catch sites at `Sync/Commands.cs:13,175,360,404`. target.md:530 lists a DIFFERENT and disjoint set (PipeMessages.cs · BridgeClient.cs · Commands.cs · PullCommandTests.cs) and does not list Program.cs at all. Two incompatible specifications share one move id; whichever the surgeon picks, the other's claims are unverified. Consequence: the commit either does not compile the described edit or does not close the described finding.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 + Check 7 (the gate is unachievable as written): target.md:534 requires the red-first test to assert `{kind:"refused"}` with EXIT 0. `CmdPull` at Program.cs:114 is `if (a.Has("--json")) { EmitJson(r); return r.Kind == ResultKinds.Ok ? 0 : 2; }` — a refused `--json` pull exits 2 and always has. The named test, written to its own spec, stays RED after the fix unless the author additionally changes CmdPull's exit-code mapping — a second, unnamed, observable change to a documented CLI contract. Consequence: either a broken gate or a silent exit-code change nobody reviewed.

moves.title: The CLI decides identity from the op's echo, not from the throttled health cache
moves.what: TWO call sites, ONE named principle, one commit. (a) `Commands.Init` derives the workspace binding — `WorkspaceConfig.Bridge.Vendor`, `Project.Platform`, `Project.ProjectName` — AND the workspace folder name from the init fetch's echoed live identity (`fetched.Platform`/`fetched.ProjectName`, produced by `OpGuard.RequireBoundProject` from live driver state), not from `bridge.GetHealth()`. The health call is kept only as the early friendly refusal ('no PLC project loaded'). Fetch first into the resolved root, THEN write config and name the folder. (b) `BridgeClient.GuardEmptyItems` decides 'was that empty fetch real' from the same echoed identity rather than a second `health` call. OLD behaviour: init writes the binding BEFORE the fetch from `[JsonIgnore]` helpers off a snapshot TwinCAT throttles to ~5s, while every later op validates against live state — so init exits 0, the folder is named `Line1`, the files are `Line2`'s, and every subsequent pull refuses WRONG_PROJECT forever; and `GuardEmptyItems` refuses a brand-new empty project the bridge just successfully walked, inside the ~5s window right after `SelectProject`. NEW behaviour: one question, one answer, at both sites. Observed by: an engineer whose very first `volt init` binds the wrong project, and one whose first contact with Volt is a refusal contradicted by the very op it guards.
moves.why: ARCHITECTURE.md convention 3 violated at the one place that decides the binding for the workspace's whole life, plus its sibling in the same file. It is also the leading candidate explanation for the parked `conflict-resolve` e2e (init succeeds, the next pull errors, both pass alone). Folding is correct because it is ONE named change — 'the CLI decides identity from the op's echo' — not two.
closes: volt init writes the workspace binding from the CACHED health snapshot while every later op validates it against the LIVE served name
BridgeClient.GuardEmptyItems decides whether an empty fetch was real by reading the throttled health cache
moves.standsAlone: Depends on move 12 for the independent `HealthSnapshotProjectName` knob without which the regression cannot be pinned. Confined to two CLI files; init's `--json` shape and exit codes are unchanged on the happy path.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test: `InitCommandTests.Init_binds_the_project_the_fetch_walked_not_the_one_the_cache_named` with `HealthSnapshotProjectName = "Line1"` and live `ServedProjectName = "Line2"`, asserting both the written binding AND the workspace folder name are `Line2`. Impossible to write today (one knob feeds both sources, so every existing init assertion is a tautology).
moves.riskiestPart: Reordering means the (potentially long) init fetch now runs before the 'that folder already exists and isn't empty' check, so a user who picks an occupied directory pays a full project walk before the refusal. The alternative — fetching after the folder exists and rewriting the config — leaves a wrongly-NAMED folder behind, which is the worse half of the bug. Second: `FetchResponse.Platform`/`ProjectName` are nullable specifically so an older bridge can omit them; init must REFUSE with a clear message on a null echo rather than binding an empty vendor, or this trades a stale binding for an empty one. Third: `PhaseProgress`'s four phases and their labels must survive the reorder intact, or the progress bar regresses in volt-control.
moves.source: minimal-move (init half) + seam-first (GuardEmptyItems half, grafted by all three judges)
objections: [invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Split it, and pick the refs answer explicitly. The init-binding fix is the valuable half and should ship alone — but only with the whole identity taken from the echo, not just the config row: run the init fetch BEFORE creating the directory (or make every error path after Directory.CreateDirectory clean up), so folder, README, commit message and binding all come from fetched.Platform/fetched.ProjectName, and re-implement the "no PLC project loaded" refusal on a null echo. Name the two deltas out loud: init now refuses "already exists and isn't empty" only after the walk, and the init commit content changes. The GuardEmptyItems half must not ride along: decide first whether the guard is still worth having, since on the echo it cannot fire on TwinCAT at all — if it can't fire, delete it and delete the class comment that promises it; if it should fire, that is a wire move (add the identity echo to RefsResponse and route refs through OpGuard) with its own parity + e2e treatment, not two CLI files. Watch above all: after the change, `volt pull` against a bridge whose TwinCAT tree walk returned zero items (BeckhoffDriver.Tree.cs:36 returns silently at the root on a COM fault, Debug-logged only) is accepted as truth and merges a deletion of every file in src/ — the empty-walk case is now unguarded on that vendor by construction.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 (observable change must be NAMED) — the refs path has no echo to read, so the move's stated mechanism cannot apply to a third of the guard's call sites, and whichever of the three possible resolutions is chosen is an unnamed behavior delta. RefsResponse (packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Engine/Wire/RefsFetch.cs:6-19) carries no platform/projectName, and RefsService.Handle (packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Engine/Sync/RefsService.cs:19-38) never calls OpGuard. Options: (a) leave GetRefs on health — `volt status` keeps false-refusing PLC_DISCONNECTED on a stale TwinCAT cache, i.e. the UI-polled path stays broken and the method now answers one question two ways INSIDE the method whose whole justification is convention 3; (b) drop the guard for refs — unnamed change to `volt status`; (c) add the echo to the wire — files and blast radius the move does not declare.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 again (init half, unnamed deltas) — Commands.cs:22-49 consumes health.ProjectName FIVE times before bridge.Init() at :57: the \"no PLC project loaded\" refusal (:22), SafeFolderName → the created directory (:28-32), SaveConfig (:38-43), the scaffold README (:45), and the `volt init: {name}` commit message (:49). Binding from the echo either (i) leaves folder/README/commit on the stale cached name while the config holds the live one — a workspace whose folder and README name a different project than its binding, with no loud error anywhere, or (ii) requires reordering init so the fetch precedes directory creation — which moves the \"already exists and isn't empty\" and \"no project loaded\" refusals to AFTER a multi-second full-project walk and changes the init commit's content (different git object SHA). The move names neither.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 (ARCHITECTURE §Conventions) — the guard becomes a check that cannot fail, while its class-level comment (BridgeClient.cs:17-18, \"never treat an empty item set as truth unless the IDE is provably attached\") keeps promising protection. Post-move it can only fire when IsConnected is true AND ServedProjectName is null: impossible on TwinCAT (IsConnected = _dte != null && _sysManager != null, and _projectName is set/cleared with _sysManager, TcObjectModel.cs:47-49, :158-183), reachable on CODESYS only for a never-saved project (CodesysObjectModel.cs:56-59). A guard that is dead on one vendor and near-dead on the other, kept with a reassuring comment, is worse than deleting it and saying so.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 (second answer not actually eliminated) — BridgeResolver.ProjectNamesOf (packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli/Sync/BridgeResolver.cs:52,:64) resolves which pipe to use by matching the BOUND name against GetHealth().Projects, i.e. the very throttled snapshot the move is removing. Sourcing the binding from the echo does not close the one-question-two-sources shape; it relocates where the two sources meet, from init-vs-pull to init-vs-resolve, and the move mentions this edge nowhere.

[invariants] objection: Checks 7 + 8 (pinning / stands alone) — the two edits are two behaviors and the gate names one red test. The stated red test (\"empty fetch with a stale cache\") is writable and covers only the GuardEmptyItems half. The init-mis-binding half CANNOT be given a red-first test with the shared double: FakeIde.HealthProjectName (test/shared/FakeIde.cs:105) is the single knob feeding both ServedProjectName (:227) and BuildHealthResponse (:240-243), and StaleHealthSnapshot (:108) can only make the cache serve NOTHING — in which case today's init refuses \"no PLC project loaded\" rather than mis-binding. Pinning it requires editing test/shared/FakeIde.cs, which is Compile-linked into three test assemblies and is a different finding's smallest fix. So the commit either ships the init half unpinned (gate claim false) or drags a shared-fake change it does not list.

[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Split it in two, and decide `refs` out loud before touching anything. (A) The BridgeClient half alone is defensible and has a real red-first test today (FakeIde StaleHealthSnapshot + zero items). But it MUST state what happens to `GetRefs`: either give `refs` the same echo — which is a wire move with its own files (Volt.Engine/Wire/RefsFetch.cs, Volt.Engine/Sync/RefsService.cs), its own e2e and its own row in the plan — or keep the health-based guard on `refs` and say so in the commit, which half-serves convention 3 but is honest. Silently deleting the guard from the `refs` path is the one outcome that must not ship: it turns `volt status` into a component that will render an empty IDE as truth. (B) The init half is a separate move, and it has to carry the FOLDER name with the binding (Commands.cs:28-29) or it creates the folder/binding split the finding it cites explicitly names. It also needs the FakeIde knob (`HealthSnapshotProjectName`) first, in its own commit, because that file compiles into three test assemblies. The one thing to watch either way: `volt-control`'s `satisfies()` matches the binding against the HEALTH row's projectName (connector.ts:50-54) — whatever init writes must still equal that row, and nothing currently pins it.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone / compiles as written) — GuardEmptyItems has THREE callers, and one of them consumes a DTO that has no echo to use. BridgeClient.cs:31-36 `GetRefs` deserializes `RefsResponse`, declared at Volt.Engine/Wire/RefsFetch.cs:6-19 with exactly four members: projectVersion, structureVersion, items, folders. There is no Platform/ProjectName. Worse, `RefsService.Handle` (RefsService.cs:19-21) does not call OpGuard at all — it does its own `if (!ide.IsConnected) throw BridgeException.PlcDisconnected()` — so the refs op does not even COMPUTE a live identity it could echo. FIRST COMPILE ERROR, unavoidable under the move's own wording: CS1061 'RefsResponse' does not contain a definition for 'ProjectName' at packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli/Sync/BridgeClient.cs:34. Consequence: the move cannot be applied inside its two named files.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (observable delta must be NAMED) — both escapes from that compile error introduce a delta the move does not name. (a) Give `refs` the echo: that adds two JSON fields to an op's response, so the blast radius is `wire`, not `cross-project`, and it requires Volt.Engine/Wire/RefsFetch.cs + Volt.Engine/Sync/RefsService.cs — neither is in the files list. (b) Drop the guard from GetRefs: `Commands.Status` (Commands.cs:119-131) wraps the refs call in a try/catch and today renders `Detail = ex.Message` when the guard fires; without it, `volt status` against a bridge with a stale/empty walk renders an ONLINE snapshot with zero items, i.e. the exact 'the engineer deleted everything' lie the guard's own doc comment (BridgeClient.cs:16-18) exists to prevent. Neither delta appears in the move.

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (ARCHITECTURE.md Conventions — one question, one answer) — the folded-in init half closes half of finding findings.md:40-52 and manufactures a NEW split with the other half. Commands.Init consumes `health.ProjectName` in six places: the 'no PLC project loaded' refusal (Commands.cs:22-23), the workspace FOLDER name (:28-29 `SafeFolderName(health.ProjectName!)`), the config binding (:41), the scaffold (:45), the reported project string (:47) and the git commit message (:49). The move's `what` says only 'the init binding'. The finding it cites explicitly names the folder ('even names the workspace FOLDER after the wrong project', findings.md:50). Leaving the folder on the cached name and moving only the binding to the live name yields folder=Line1 / binding=Line2 — two answers to one question, created at the exact call site the move claims to unify.

[mechanics] objection: Check 8 again (the big-bang hiding inside) — moving the binding to `fetched.*` forces a restructure of Commands.Init, not an edit. `SaveConfig` is at :38-43; `var fetched = bridge.Init(...)` is at :57. The naive edit produces a SECOND compile error, CS0841 'Cannot use local variable fetched before it is declared', at Commands.cs:40-41. Doing it properly means hoisting the fetch above Directory.CreateDirectory (:32), Git.GitInit (:35), SaveConfig (:38), Scaffold (:45) and Git.CommitAll (:49) — which also moves the cheap 'folder already exists and isn't empty' refusal (:30-31) to AFTER a full IDE walk. That is an observable latency/ordering change (seconds of frozen IDE before a refusal that is currently instant) in code that elsewhere goes out of its way to avoid an unnecessary walk (see the localOnly rationale, Commands.cs:107-112). Unnamed.

[mechanics] objection: Check 7 (red-first test) — half-satisfiable. The named test ('empty fetch with a stale cache') IS writable today: FakeIde `StaleHealthSnapshot = true` with zero items makes BuildHealthResponse report nothing serving (FakeIde.cs:240-243) while ServedProjectName stays live (:227), so GuardEmptyItems throws PLC_DISCONNECTED — red before, green after. But that test pins only the BridgeClient half. The init half's actual failure — the cached row naming a DIFFERENT project — is unrepresentable in the shared double: FakeIde.cs:105 has ONE knob (`HealthProjectName`) feeding BOTH the live signal (:227) and the cached row (:242), and findings.md:55-67 states this in terms ('Phase 5 will fix the init binding and have no way to prove it stays fixed'). Fixing it needs a new knob in test/shared/FakeIde.cs — a file `<Compile Include>`-linked into THREE test assemblies (findings.md:145-157). Not in the file list, not in the gate.

moves.what: Add a `RefsRequest { ExpectedPlatform, ExpectedProjectName }` to `Wire/RefsFetch.cs` — both nullable, so a body-less `refs` behaves exactly as today and the TS e2e harness (which sends `refs` with no body) is unaffected. `RefsService.Handle` takes it and replaces its bare `if (!ide.IsConnected)` with `OpGuard.RequireBoundProject(ide, req?.ExpectedPlatform, req?.ExpectedProjectName)`. `BridgeClient.GetRefs` sends the workspace's bound identity. `Commands.Status`'s pre-op `Config.ProjectMismatch(cfg, health)` guard is DELETED; the mismatch verdict now comes from the WRONG_PROJECT refusal the op itself raises, rendered through the existing mismatch path — `Commands.Status` must catch that refusal and produce the SAME rendered output. OLD behaviour: `refs` is the only project-touching op with no identity on the wire, so `volt status` guards it by reading the throttled health cache — the exact pattern `OpGuard`'s own doc and convention 3 forbid, one wire-hop out from where it was fixed; and the two spellings disagree on case (`OrdinalIgnoreCase` in `OpGuard`, `!=` in `Config`). NEW behaviour: one question, one answer. Observed by: an engineer on a two-project XAE right after a rebind, whose `volt status` today walks the OTHER project and renders every tracked file as incoming-removed and every foreign file as incoming-added — a full-project phantom diff on a live PLC repo — while `volt pull` in the same second refuses WRONG_PROJECT.

closes: refs is the only project-touching op with no identity on the wire, so volt status guards it with a pre-op read of the throttled health cache

moves.what: Put the four strings of the `Connector.Core → VoltBridgeTwincat.exe` contract — `--list-xae-pids`, `--xae-pid`, the exit-code meanings, one-pid-per-line stdout — in one const table in `Volt.Cli.Transport` (the project that already owns `Ops` for exactly this reason), and have both `Volt.Cli.Connector.Core/TwincatXaeProbe.cs` and `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat/Program.cs` reference it. Both projects already reference Transport. No behaviour changes: same flags, same exit codes, same parsing.
moves.why: Closes the certain finding that `Connector.Core` — whose csproj comment says 'pure logic + the pipe wire' — reaches the TwinCAT IDE host by an UNTYPED process CLI with no ProjectReference between them. Rename `--list-xae-pids` to `--xae-pids` in `Program.cs:19` and `dotnet build`, all three C# suites and `bun run check` stay green while at runtime the child exits non-zero, `ListPids` returns null, `TwincatSupervisor` reads that as 'probe failed — leave the fleet alone', and an engineer who opens a new XAE never gets a worker: TwinCAT silently stops syncing, permanently. This is also the only pinnable seam for move 23, since no test project can reference `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat`.
closes: Volt.Cli.Connector.Core — the project whose csproj says its only dependency is the pipe wire — reaches the TwinCAT IDE host by process CLI, past IProjectSource and past the compiler
moves.standsAlone: Both projects already reference `Volt.Cli.Transport`, so no csproj changes. Replacing two string literals on each side with the same const is behaviour-identical by construction. Kept SEPARATE from move 23 deliberately: bundling a const-table extraction with a named exit-code semantics change is a fix move wearing a costume.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites. Add a `TwincatXaeProbeTests` case that compiles against the const table, so a rename becomes a build error rather than a silent permanent 'no TwinCAT bridge is running'.
moves.riskiestPart: The table must go in Transport, not in Connector.Core — putting it in Connector.Core would make the IDE host reference the connector, inverting the graph. moves.title: A partial XAE enumeration fails the probe instead of reaping a healthy worker
moves.what: `RotInstances.EnumeratePids` gains a completeness verdict: a per-DTE failure on a moniker that IS a DTE (`IsDteMoniker` matched) and whose pid read failed — `PidOf`'s swallowed catch, `EnumRunningDtesOnce`'s per-moniker `continue` — makes the enumeration incomplete, and `Program.cs`'s `--list-xae-pids` branch exits non-zero. A NON-DTE moniker is not evidence of anything and does not fail the probe. `TwincatXaeProbe.ListPids` already reads non-zero as 'probe failed → leave the fleet untouched', so nothing above changes. OLD behaviour: the contract is stated twice as 'exit 0 = the enumeration RAN', but `PidOf` is a cross-process COM call into the XAE's UI thread that swallows everything and returns 0, so a busy XAE — one pinned by a `volt push` or a full `volt build` for tens of seconds, the normal case on a large project — silently vanishes from a list that still exits 0. `TwincatSupervisor` reaps after 3 misses at ~12s apiece, so ~36s of a busy XAE kills a perfectly healthy worker. NEW behaviour: an incomplete probe reaps nothing. Observed by: an engineer mid-push whose pipe disappears, whose in-flight op dies with 'bridge is not reachable', and whose respawned worker comes up with NO project bound — after which a terminal-only user gets PLC_DISCONNECTED on every command until they open a GUI.
moves.why: This is the reap path for the exact workflow ARCHITECTURE.md's disconnect section protects ('the CLI opens the pipe directly and never consults the connector'), and it is a leading candidate for the parked e2e: the run-alone case never accumulates 36s of continuous XAE-busy time; the full suite does.
closes: --list-xae-pids conflates "the enumeration ran" with "every live XAE answered": a busy XAE is silently dropped from the list and the probe still exits 0, so the supervisor reaps a healthy worker
moves.standsAlone: Depends on move 22 for the const table. Contained to the file that owns the flag plus its one-shot entry point; `TwincatXaeProbe`, `TwincatSupervisor` and `TrayContext` are unchanged — they already implement the contract this restores.
moves.gate: Build + all three suites, PLUS a NAMED RED-FIRST test on the CONSUMER seam: `TwincatXaeProbeTests.A_probe_child_that_exits_non_zero_reaps_nothing`, driven by a stub exe. The PRODUCER half (`RotInstances`) cannot be pinned offline — no test .csproj references `Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat` and it is net8.0-windows, so a net8.0 test project structurally cannot. Its safety argument is MONOTONICITY, stated plainly in the commit: the change can only make the probe more conservative — strictly fewer reaps, never more. Plus a live check against two XAE windows, one busy and one idle.
moves.riskiestPart: Over-strictness in the other direction: if some ROT entry on a given machine ALWAYS fails to answer (a stale moniker, a zombie DTE), every probe becomes incomplete, the fleet is never reaped, and a closed XAE's worker lingers — trading a rare wrong reap for a possible permanent stall. The `IsDteMoniker` bound is the mitigation. If a permanently-unreadable DTE entry proves reachable in practice, the fallback is exit 2 while still printing the readable pids, with `ListPids` treating 2 as 'partial → do not reap, but do spawn'.

objections:
[mechanics] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: If the majority lets this through, the surgeon must carry three objections. (1) The file list is wrong and must be corrected to target.md's — RotInstances.cs + Program.cs + TwincatXaeProbeTests.cs — with TwincatSupervisor.cs REMOVED; touching Reconcile is a second, unnamed behavior change that breaks TwincatSupervisorTests.cs:52 and :75, and no finding asks for it. Leave PidOf:27-37 exactly as it is (BindByPid:47 and TcObjectModel.cs:63/78/108 depend on its per-window tolerance) and put the completeness verdict ONLY in EnumeratePids' own loop, as a separate out-parameter or a new method, so the probe path tightens and the worker's re-attach path does not. The narrower form that would actually be safe, and that I would not refute: land move 22 (worker-cli-const-table) first, then ship ONLY the producer change as a new `RotInstances.TryEnumeratePids(out List<int> pids)` that leaves `EnumeratePids`, `PidOf` and `BindByPid` byte-identical, with Program.cs:19-31 switching to it and returning the const-table's failure code — one file's worth of new code, one call site, zero changes to any shared symbol, and no test edited. [mechanics] objection: Check 8 (stands alone) — the move's OWN justification field is a dependency statement: 'Depends on worker-cli-const-table for the exit-code vocabulary', and target.md row 23 repeats it verbatim ('Stands alone. Depends on move 22 for the const table'). After this commit and nothing else, the exit-code vocabulary it is written against does not exist. [mechanics] objection: Check 8 / compile reality — the file list is RotInstances.cs + TwincatSupervisor.cs, and it omits the ONLY production caller of the symbol being changed. Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat/Program.cs:24 is `foreach (var id in RotInstances.EnumeratePids()) Console.WriteLine(id);`. Consequence: FIRST COMPILE ERROR = CS1579 at packages/volt-cli/src/Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat/Program.cs:24 ('foreach statement cannot operate on variables of type (List<int>, bool) because it does not contain a public instance definition for GetEnumerator') the moment EnumeratePids returns a completeness verdict alongside the list. The producer is structurally untestable offline: Volt.Cli.Ide.Twincat is net8.0-windows Exe, and Volt.Cli.Tests:3, Volt.Engine.Tests:3 and Volt.Cli.Connector.Tests:3 are all net8.0 (NU1201). Consequence: the named red-first test cannot be written red, which is why the move substituted a 'MONOTONICITY gate in TwincatSupervisor' — see next item.

A gate weak enough not to break them cannot be red-first either.

[mechanics] objection: Check 1 (observable change must be NAMED) — the move names the probe exit-code delta, but TwincatSupervisor.cs is in its file list while target.md row 23 states 'TwincatXaeProbe, TwincatSupervisor and TrayContext are unchanged'. Consequence: the reap-policy delta in the supervisor is an UNNAMED second observable behavior change in a component whose whole job is deciding when to kill a live worker.

[mechanics] objection: Check 2 (per-entry tolerance in a foreign-process COM walk) — RotInstances.PidOf:27 has two consumers with OPPOSITE requirements: EnumeratePids:61 (the probe, which the move wants strict) and BindByPid:47 (the worker's own re-attach, reached from TcObjectModel.cs:63/78/108, which MUST skip a busy OTHER window to find its own). Consequence: making PidOf strict/throwing means one busy neighbouring XAE stops the worker re-acquiring ITS OWN window, producing the same PLC_DISCONNECTED the move exists to prevent. This is the same family as Beckhoff's per-node try/catch in the tree walk — per-entry tolerance in a foreign-process enumeration — and the move's file list gives no sign the author noticed the shared consumer.

[mechanics] objection: Check 4 (second answer to one question / vocabulary) — target.md's own stated fallback is 'exit 2 while still printing the readable pids, with ListPids treating 2 as partial → do not reap, but do spawn'. TwincatXaeProbe.ListPids returns IReadOnlyList<int>? — a two-state type (null=failed, list=ran) that cannot express a third 'partial' state. Consequence: the fallback silently requires changing ListPids' return type and TrayContext.cs:153-159, neither of which is in the file list, and creates a third exit-code meaning with no home in the const table move 22 is supposed to own.

[mechanics] objection: Check 5 / blind spot — the completeness verdict is bounded by IsDteMoniker, but EnumRunningDtesOnce:103-104 catches a GetDisplayName failure and `continue`s BEFORE IsDteMoniker is ever evaluated. Consequence: a moniker whose display-name read fails can never be classified as a DTE, so it remains a silent partial drop that the fix structurally cannot close — the finding is only partially closed, not closed.

[invariants] REQUIRED AMENDMENT: Carry this objection: the safety claim "strictly fewer reaps, never more" is not the whole monotonicity story, and the majority must not accept it as written. The same `return` that suppresses a reap (TrayContext.cs:154) also suppresses `EnsureWorker` for every pid, which is spawn AND crash-restart — undebounced, on the first failed probe, while the reap it prevents cost three. Watch for exactly this in the field: XAE B opened during a long build in XAE A never gets `volt.bridge.twincat.<pidB>`, and no log line says why.

The narrower form that would be safe, and that keeps one owner for one question: leave RotInstances' per-DTE catches intact and have `EnumeratePids` return the incompleteness ALONGSIDE the pids — worker exits 2 and still prints the readable pids (target.md move 23 already names this as its fallback; make it the primary). Then `TwincatXaeProbe.ListPids` gains a third verdict — 0 = complete, 2 = partial, anything else = failed — and TrayContext spawns from a partial list while skipping the reap branch only. That preserves discovery and crash-restart, does not co-own the debounce, does not touch TwincatSupervisor at all, and lands the red-first test where target.md actually puts it: `TwincatXaeProbeTests` driven by a stub exe asserting exit 2 → pids returned, reap suppressed — a test that is genuinely red today and needs no edit to any existing green test. It also makes the worker-cli-const-table dependency real instead of decorative, since exit 2 would then be vocabulary two projects share. Scope must include Program.cs and TwincatXaeProbe.cs; the row's two-file list cannot deliver this and should be rewritten before anyone opens an editor.

[invariants] objection: Check 7 — the named gate is structurally unwritable, and making it writable forces edits to green tests. The row's gate is "a MONOTONICITY gate in TwincatSupervisor is the testable surface". TwincatSupervisor never observes the thing this move changes: TrayContext.cs:154 is `if (pids == null) return;` — it returns BEFORE `_twincatSupervisor.Reconcile(pids)` at :155. A failed probe never reaches the supervisor, so no input to `Reconcile` differs before vs. after the fix and any test written there is GREEN before the fix (not red-first). To make it red you must add a NEW monotonicity mechanism inside TwincatSupervisor — a second, unnamed behavior change — and that mechanism collides head-on with an existing green test: TwincatSupervisorTests.cs:51-61 `A_sustained_absence_reaps_the_worker_after_N_misses` feeds exactly a shrinking pid set (Pids(100) → Pids() ×3) and asserts a reap. A gate that refuses to act on a shrunk set turns that test red for a reason independent of the defect. Consequence: the move ships with no red-first evidence at all, or it ships with an edited oracle.

[invariants] objection: Check 1 — the fix has a SECOND observable delta that is not named, and it is larger than the named one. The row names "a partial enumeration fails the probe". It does not name the consequence that TrayContext.cs:151-159 skips `_supervisor.EnsureWorker(...)` for EVERY pid on the same null return, and EnsureWorker is not just spawn — BridgeSupervisor.cs:36-40 restarts a CRASHED worker (`if (!existing.HasExited) return; Log.Warn("worker {id} crashed — restarting")`), which TrayContext.cs:146-148 documents as load-bearing. So one non-answering XAE also (a) blocks a newly-opened XAE from ever getting a worker or a pipe, and (b) disables crash-recovery for every other worker. Worse, the reap it prevents was debounced by ReapAfterMisses=3 (~36s); this spawn/respawn suppression has NO debounce — it bites on the FIRST failed probe. The gate's whole safety argument ("strictly fewer reaps, never more") is therefore false as stated: conservative on reaps, aggressive on discovery.

[invariants] objection: Check 4 — second answer to one question. TwincatSupervisor.cs:19-21 already OWNS this exact question, in its own words: "Consecutive ticks an XAE must be ABSENT before its worker is reaped — a transient ROT gap (a busy DTE momentarily not enumerable) must not tear down a healthy worker." The move installs a second, differently-layered owner of "is this XAE really gone?", and the row's TwincatSupervisor.cs edit installs a third.
